docs.title: SafeRS Native Public API
docs.text:
This site documents the public SafeRS scripting API. Scripts are .lua files run by the client's built-in Lua VM; they call srs.<module>.<method>(args) (plus a few global tables such as entity, npc and game). Each page in the API Reference lists one module's functions, the values they return, and examples.

Threading and spoofing contract

All action-firing methods (interact, attack, click, cast, …) route through Interact on the engine main thread with always-on input spoofing. There is no escape hatch — firing engine actions from the render thread crashes, and the spoofer is fail-closed (if it can't inject, the action drops).

docs.title: Callback registration
docs.text:
script.pulse(function() ... end)     -- per frame
script.onTick(function() ... end)    -- per game tick
script.nextTick(function() ... end)  -- one-shot, fires on the next tick only
script.draw(function() ... end)      -- per frame, inside ImGui frame

script.draw is the only callback where srs.draw.* calls are valid — the host guarantees a live ImGui frame for it. pulse, onTick, and nextTick do not.

There is no script.onLoad: a Lua script's top-level chunk is its load hook. Note that the chunk runs when the script is installed (the sidebar's Load), which may be long before the user starts it with the Enabled checkbox — see Install vs start before putting start-of-run work at the top of a file.

docs.title: Metadata and settings
docs.text: A script can declare display metadata (name, author, version, description) and a settings schema that the launcher's sidebar renders as an editable form.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Without a metadata declaration, a Lua script shows up in the sidebar under its filename stem with v * * "lua" and empty version / size. To override, call script.declareInfo once at the top level:

script.declareInfo {
    name        = "Power Miner",        -- overrides filename stem
    author      = "you",
    version     = "1.0.0",
    description = "Mines essence at Power-mine, drops at threshold.",
}

All fields are optional.

docs.title: Settings schema
docs.text:
script.declareSettings takes a list of groups, each with a list of rows. The launcher renders each row as a typed input (check, select, number, slider, text, button) and ships the user's edits back to the script.

script.declareSettings {
    groups = {
        { id = "general", title = "general", open = true, rows = {
            { id = "mode",      label = "Protect mode",   kind = "select",
              value = "Auto", options = { "Auto", "Magic", "Range", "Melee" } },
            { id = "lookahead", label = "Tick lookahead", kind = "number",
              value = 1, min = 0, max = 3 },
            { id = "smite",     label = "Use Smite",      kind = "check",
              value = false },
        }},
        { id = "display", title = "display", open = true, rows = {
            { id = "opacity",   label = "Overlay opacity", kind = "slider",
              value = 80, min = 0, max = 100 },
        }},
    },
}
kind Renders as Extra fields check checkbox value: bool select dropdown value, options: [...] number numeric input value, min, max slider slider value, min, max text text box value: string, placeholder, maxLength, mono button button (no stored value) value = caption, action — handled by script.onSettingsButton

number and slider also accept step and suffix. See PluginSettings for writing values back from a button handler.

Without a declareSettings call, the sidebar shows just the master enable toggle and no rows.

docs.title: Reading values
docs.text:
User edits are flattened by the launcher to "<groupId>.<rowId>" keys before crossing the IPC boundary, so a script reads its own setting under that combined key:

script.onSettingsChanged(function(s)
    print("protect mode:", s["general.mode"])
    print("smite on:",     s["general.smite"])
end)

-- Snapshot read at call time:
local s = script.settings()
if s["general.smite"] then ... end

The launcher pushes the current values to the script on enable, on every edit, and after a hot reload — handlers should be idempotent.

Identity

A script's settings are persisted by the launcher under the script's id, derived from the filename stem. Renaming the .lua file orphans its saved values. Pick a name you're willing to keep, and avoid renaming group / row ids in the schema between releases for the same reason.

docs.title: pulse vs onTick
docs.text:
Callback Cadence Use for pulse every rendered frame (~60 Hz) cheap state checks, per-frame visual work onTick every game tick (~600 ms) action firing, state-machine transitions

Move action logic to onTick and use pulse only for checks.

docs.title: nextTick
docs.text:
nextTick bridges fast pulse detection to server-aligned firing: evaluate a condition inside pulse (~60Hz so you don't miss a short-lived window), and when it fires, queue a closure to run on the very next game tick, then drop it.

Each call queues exactly one callback. The host drains the queue once per tick after the regular onTick fan, so steady-state tick handlers always run first. A re-queue from inside a deferred callback lands on the next tick, not this one.

Property Behavior Cadence one-shot — fires on the next tick rollover, then dropped Order after onTick, before the BreakManager scheduler Pause / disable owning script disabled or paused before drain → callback is silently dropped (same gating as pulse / onTick) Re-entrancy nextTick called from inside a deferred fn schedules for the NEXT tick ImGui frame not guaranteed — call srs.draw.* only from script.draw

When to use each:

  • Always firing every tick? Use onTick.
  • Need fast detection (a projectile, a hitsplat, a tick-aligned animation start) but the action itself must land aligned to the server? Detect in pulse, defer with nextTick.
  • Per-frame visual work? Use pulse (state) + draw (paint).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Detect the "tick-eat" window in pulse (need ≥60Hz to catch it),
-- then fire the eat exactly once on the next tick.
local pending = false
script.pulse(function()
    if not pending and srs.player.hpPercent() < 35 then
        pending = true
        script.nextTick(function()
            srs.inventory.interact("Shark", "Eat")
            pending = false
        end)
    end
end)

The pending flag prevents queueing the same action 36× across the ~600 ms tick window before nextTick actually fires. Without it, every pulse between detection and the next tick would push another copy of the closure onto the queue.

Re-query inside the deferred function

The deferred function runs on a later tick, and it is dropped if the script is disabled or paused before then. Targets returned by finders (srs.npc.nearest, entity.*, …) are snapshots of the moment you queried them — look the target up again inside the deferred function rather than acting on one captured earlier.

docs.title: Example — minimal Lua script
docs.text:
-- Drop every shrimp the moment it lands in the backpack.
script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.contains("Shrimps") then
        srs.inventory.dropAll("Shrimps")
    end
end)

script.draw(function()
    if srs.draw.beginAnchoredOverlay(
            "##fish-hud", 162, 32,
            srs.Corner.TopRight, -4, 4) then
        srs.draw.text("Caught: " .. srs.inventory.count("Shrimps"))
        srs.draw.endOverlay()
    end
end)

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
srs.actions

Two halves of one problem — did the action I asked for actually happen?

Half Surface Question it answers Pre-dispatch batch / budgetRemaining / pending / cancelAll Can this tick still afford the action, and did each step in my ladder get spent? Post-dispatch lastTicket / outcome / info / verify / state Did the action I already spent reach the server, and did it take effect?

Both halves live on the srs.actions table and are documented on this page.

Scripts MUST NOT block

Verifiers are pumped once per game tick on the script thread, before your script.onTick runs. Nothing here waits or spins. You fire an action, register a verifier, and read srs.actions.state(handle) whenever you like.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Each function has its own section below.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
Across the API a true return means "the click was enqueued", never "the action happened". The Dialogue docs already say this outright; it is equally true of interactions, walks and widget clicks. Three failures live past that return and used to be indistinguishable from success:

  • the per-tick budget gate holds the action so it fires several ticks late, against a world that has moved on;
  • the action is drained, the engine's action dispatch no-ops, and no packet ever reaches the wire — the "Drop click silently did nothing" bug;
  • the queue is cleared on script stop before the action ran.

Every script therefore grew its own poll-and-retry ladder. srs.actions replaces them.

docs.title: What the engine can and cannot confirm
docs.text:
There is no per-action acknowledgement in the OSRS protocol, and there cannot be one. The outbound action packets carry no request id, sequence number or client token for a reply to reference — OpNpc1 is 4 bytes (index + control), OpLoc1 is 8 (id + x + y + control). A server reply has nothing to name.

So:

  • sent means "reached the wire", never "the server accepted it."
  • Acceptance is confirmed by observing game state — which is exactly what verify{confirm = ...} is for.
  • The strongest negative signal is the game-message channel, and that is a correlation, not an acknowledgement: a rejection is attributed to the most recent action that reached the wire within a 2-tick window.

docs.title: Same-tick batching
docs.text:
srs.actions.batch is the pre-dispatch half: it lands several actions inside one game tick, and tells you which ones the tick could not afford.

local b = srs.actions.batch({
    { "dodge",  function() srs.walk.to(x, y) end },
    { "pray",   function() srs.prayer.setActive(p, true) end,
      tab = srs.tab.PRAYER },
    { "eat",    function() srs.inventory.interactById(food, "Eat") end,
      tab = srs.tab.INVENTORY },
    { "attack", function() srs.npc.attack(boss) end },
}, {
    onDone = function(r)
        if not r.complete then
            for _, e in ipairs(r.missed) do
                print(e.label .. " never fired: " .. e.status)
            end
        end
    end,
})

docs.title: Why a ladder needs a runner at all
docs.text:
One action per rendered frame is a hard engine floor, not a pacing preference:

  1. Every scripted action primes a click, and a newly staged click replaces any earlier one that has not been consumed yet — the engine has one click slot pair.
  2. At most one staged click is consumed per dispatcher tick (~50/s, i.e. once per rendered frame), so at most one click is emitted per frame.
  3. The engine fires at most one queued action per frame, and only when that click is emitted.

So firing two actions in one frame does not get you two actions — the second click overwrites the first, one lambda is left in the paired queue with no click to drain against, and it leaks into a later tick. A frame is ~16 ms and a tick is ~600 ms, so a paced ladder still fits ~30 actions per tick; the real limit is the server's cap, below.

docs.title: The per-tick cap, and what a tab switch costs
docs.text:
The server processes at most 8 action-class packets per game cycle (srs.engine.actionLimit()). Over-cap packets are dropped, not queued.

A sidebar tab switch is one of those 8. Clicking a chrome tab is an ordinary action packet, no different from clicking an item. A ladder that hops prayer → inventory → prayer therefore spends 3 of its 8 slots on sidebar management alone — prefer a resting tab and let the runner coalesce consecutive steps that share one.

The engine's own per-tick budget gate defers an over-cap action to a later drain. For a tick-scoped ladder that is the wrong answer — the deferred attack lands two ticks late. The batch runner instead fails fast: a step that does not fit is never dispatched, and comes back as gated.

docs.title: srs.actions.batch(steps[, opts]) -> handle
docs.text:
steps is an ordered list. Each entry is a function, or a table:

Field Meaning [1] / label Short name, echoed in the report. Defaults to stepN. [2] / fn The action. Return false for "I chose not to act" so the step is not charged a slot; anything else (including no return) counts as dispatched. tab Sidebar tab that must be open first, e.g. srs.tab.PRAYER. Omit for "don't care".

One step = one action packet

Two clicks inside one fn means the second overwrites the first's staged click and never reaches the server. Split them into two steps.

opts:

Field Default Meaning tickScoped true Steps still unrun when the tick rolls are dropped and reported expired, rather than fired at a world that has moved on. Set false for ladders that are safe to finish late (bank flows, prep). reserve 0 Keep this many action slots free for whatever runs after the batch. tabSettleFrames 2 Frames to let the engine draw a newly switched panel before clicking into it. The tab flips synchronously, but the panel's drawn rectangle is a frame behind. onDone — Called once when the batch retires, with the report.

The handle has :report(), :done(), :cancel() and .id.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
{
  id = 7, finished = true, complete = false,
  dispatched = 6, noOp = 0, gated = 2, expired = 0, failed = 0, cancelled = 0,
  tabSwitches = 2,
  steps  = { { label = "dodge", status = "dispatched", missed = false, tabCost = 0 }, ... },
  missed = { { label = "attack", status = "gated", missed = true, tabCost = 0 } },
}

status is one of dispatched, noop, gated, expired, cancelled, failed (or pending for a step not yet reached, in a report read before the batch finishes). missed lists exactly the steps that never reached the wire — that is the list to reprioritise from on the next tick.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
If a step names a tab, the runner switches to it, waits for it to read open, waits tabSettleFrames for the panel to be drawn, and only then runs the step. Consecutive steps naming the same tab share one switch. A step already on its tab costs nothing.

If srs.tab.current() is unreadable (Unknown — the VarClient read is unavailable), the runner does not refuse to act: it switches once blind, settles, and proceeds. Refusing would strand the whole ladder, which is strictly worse than clicking after a switch.

docs.title: srs.actions.budgetRemaining([reserve]) -> integer
docs.text: Action slots believed usable this tick. Unlike srs.engine.actionsSentThisTick(), this also counts actions the runner has dispatched whose packets have not reached the wire yet, so it never over-reports capacity.

docs.title: srs.actions.pending() -> integer
docs.text: Batches in flight.

docs.title: srs.actions.cancelAll()
docs.text: Flags every in-flight batch for cancellation. Remaining steps report cancelled. Batches are also dropped automatically when the script that submitted them is disabled or reloaded.

docs.title: Dispatch tickets
docs.text:
Every marshaled action gets a ticket. Ask for it straight after the call:

srs.inventory.interactById(id, "Drop")
local t = srs.actions.lastTicket()

docs.title: srs.actions.lastTicket() -> integer
docs.text: Ticket for the most recent action requested on this thread. 0 = the call marshaled nothing.

docs.title: srs.actions.outcome(ticket) -> string
docs.text: Outcome Meaning pending queued, not yet drained — the budget gate may be holding it sent drained, and an action-class packet went out noPacket drained but produced no packet — the silent no-op noDispatch the API bailed before anything was queued discarded the queue was cleared before it ran (script stop / cancel) expired never drained; aged out unknown no such ticket, or it fell off the 512-row history

docs.title: srs.actions.sent(ticket) -> boolean
docs.text: outcome == "sent".

docs.title: srs.actions.failed(ticket) -> boolean
docs.text: The action definitively never reached the server. False while still pending, so it is safe to poll.

docs.title: srs.actions.info(ticket) -> table | nil
docs.text:
{ ticket, outcome, kind, a, b, packets, queuedTicks, ageTicks }
  • kind — "widget", "object", "npc", "player", "tile", "clickFire", or "action" (an interaction with no more specific kind).
  • a / b — kind-specific ids (item id, group/child, npc id + spawn index).
  • packets — action-class packets observed while it ran; 0 = noPacket.
  • queuedTicks — server ticks the budget gate held it before it drained. Non-zero means you queued more actions in a tick than the server's 8-per-tick cap allows and this one landed late.

docs.title: srs.actions.recent([n]) -> list
docs.text: Last n ledger rows (default 16), oldest first. Returns a proper Lua table of info rows.

docs.title: srs.actions.queued() -> integer
docs.text: Ledger tickets enqueued but not yet drained. (Distinct from srs.actions.pending(), which counts batch-runner steps.)

docs.title: srs.actions.oldestPendingTicks() -> integer
docs.text: How long the longest-waiting queued action has been held. A steadily rising number means you are out-running the server's action cap — back off rather than queue more.

docs.title: srs.actions.stats() -> table
docs.text: { opened, sent, noPacket, discarded } — lifetime counters, for HUDs.

docs.title: srs.actions.rejections([n]) -> list
docs.text:
Last n rejection rows (default 8), oldest first.

{ text, reason, ticket, tick }

reason is a classifier label: materials, space, reach, level, noop, refused. ticket is the correlated action, or 0 when none could own it. Only server/system channels are read — player chat can never be mistaken for a rejection.

docs.title: srs.actions.verify(spec) -> handle
docs.text:
Non-blocking poll-and-retry.

srs.inventory.interactById(id, "Drop")

local h = srs.actions.verify{
    kind    = "drop",
    ticket  = srs.actions.lastTicket(),
    confirm = function() return not srs.inventory.contains(id) end,
    retry   = function() return srs.inventory.interactById(id, "Drop") end,
}

-- later, from onTick:
if srs.actions.state(h) == "failed" then ... end
Field Default Meaning confirm required Truthy = the action took effect. Called once per tick — keep it a cheap state read, never an action. retry — Re-dispatch. Called at most attempts - 1 times. onDone — Called once with (state, detail) when resolved. ticket 0 From lastTicket(). See below — this is what makes the helper better than a hand-rolled timer. reject built-in classifier List of server-message substrings (or a single string) meaning "give up now". kind "" Label, surfaced in check(h).kind. waitTicks 3 Ticks to wait for confirm before retrying. attempts 3 Total dispatches allowed, counting the original.

Pass the ticket. When it resolves noPacket / noDispatch / discarded, the retry fires immediately instead of burning the rest of the waitTicks window waiting for a confirmation that was never coming. A still-pending ticket is not a failure — that is the budget gate holding it.

Resolution order each tick: confirm → rejection → dispatch outcome → wait window. A confirmed outcome always wins over a rejection guess.

docs.title: srs.actions.state(handle) -> string
docs.text: pending | confirmed | rejected | failed | unknown. Resolved handles stay readable for ~20 ticks, then report unknown.

docs.title: srs.actions.done(handle) -> boolean
docs.text: True once the verifier has resolved (confirmed, rejected or failed).

docs.title: srs.actions.check(handle) -> table | nil
docs.text:
{ state, detail, kind, ticket, attempts, ageTicks }

detail says why it ended: the rejection text, the dispatch outcome, or "not confirmed within the retry budget".

docs.title: srs.actions.cancel(handle) -> boolean
docs.text: Stop verifying; the handle resolves failed with detail "cancelled". Returns false if the handle is unknown or already resolved.

docs.title: srs.actions.verifying() -> integer
docs.text: How many verifiers are still pending.

docs.title: Worked example: a bowl craft that the server refuses
docs.text:
The spend is the confirmation — the crafted item sometimes never reads as owned, but the shards always leave.

local before = srs.inventory.count(shardId)
srs.widget.click(270, 21, "Make")

srs.actions.verify{
    kind      = "make:staff",
    ticket    = srs.actions.lastTicket(),
    confirm   = function() return srs.inventory.count(shardId) <= before - 50 end,
    attempts  = 1,          -- the ladder re-decides next tick; a retry would double-craft
    waitTicks = 8,
    onDone    = function(state, detail)
        if state == "confirmed" then made = true
        else log.info("make " .. state .. ": " .. detail) end
    end,
}

When the server answers "You do not have the materials required to make that." the verifier resolves rejected on the tick the line arrives — instead of waiting out eight ticks for a spend that was never coming — and the ticket still reads sent, so you can tell "the server refused it" from "the click never landed". Those are different bugs.

docs.title: Antiban
docs.text:
srs.antiban

Human-like timing + idle behavior. Designed for onTick:

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.antiban.shouldDelay()      then return end
    if srs.antiban.shouldMicroBreak() then return end
    if workIsDone() then
        srs.antiban.moveMouseRandomly()
        return
    end
    performAction()
    srs.antiban.recordAction()
end)

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Lua Record an action timestamp srs.antiban.recordAction() Ms since last action srs.antiban.idleTimeMs() → int Idle past threshold (default 5m) srs.antiban.isIdleTooLong(thresholdMs?) → bool Probabilistic action-skip (default 5%) srs.antiban.shouldDelay(fatigue?) → bool Probabilistic micro-break (default 0.1%) srs.antiban.shouldMicroBreak(prob?) → bool Drift mouse to random screen point srs.antiban.moveMouseRandomly() → bool Park mouse on a random point of the canvas edge srs.antiban.moveMouseOffScreen() → bool Total delays skipped srs.antiban.totalDelaysSkipped() → int Total micro-breaks srs.antiban.totalMicroBreaks() → int Total random moves srs.antiban.totalRandomMoves() → int

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• shouldDelay's fatigue argument is the per-call skip probability (0..1). Default 5%; pass higher values during long sessions to slow the script down.
  • shouldMicroBreak's default of 0.1 % is per call: roughly one break per ~16 seconds when polled at 60 Hz (pulse), but only about one per ~10 minutes when polled once per game tick from onTick as in the example above. Raise prob for per-tick use.
  • idleTimeMs returns 0 and isIdleTooLong returns false until the first recordAction() call.
  • moveMouseRandomly picks its point inside the live viewport, read from the engine's internal camera state; it falls back to (1024, 768) if the camera hasn't initialized yet.
  • The three total* counters are diagnostic — they feed the debug panel readout and are handy for script HUDs / logging.

docs.title: Area
docs.text:
srs.area

Player-position area-containment checks, plus the WorldTile and WorldArea geometry value types. The isWithin player checks are 2D only (plane ignored); the WorldArea value type is plane-aware.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Inside inclusive rect srs.area.isWithin(x1, y1, x2, y2) → bool Within Chebyshev radius srs.area.isWithin(cx, cy, tilesAway) → bool In an instance srs.area.isInInstance() → bool Rectangle area srs.area.rect(x1, y1, x2, y2[, plane]) / srs.area.rect(cornerA, cornerB) → WorldArea Circular area srs.area.circle(cx, cy, r[, plane]) / srs.area.circle(centerTile, r) → WorldArea
  • Rect form — (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) are opposing corners. Either pair works (upper-left + lower-right, upper-right + lower-left, etc.) — internally min/max-ed against each axis.
  • Radius form — tilesAway is inclusive (player on the boundary counts as inside). tilesAway = 0 means "exactly on the tile".

Lua dispatches by arity: 4 args = rect, 3 args = radius.

isInInstance returns true when the current scene is a real instance (a private boss arena, raid, minigame lobby, …), read from the engine's in-instance flag; false when that flag can't be resolved. Pairs with srs.player.templatePosition() for instance-aware coordinate handling.

docs.title: WorldTile
docs.text:
A world coordinate value type — now constructible with tile-math helpers, so scripts stop hand-rolling coordinate arithmetic. Also returned by srs.player.position() and the entity/tile APIs.

Method Lua Construct WorldTile.new(x, y) / WorldTile.new(x, y, plane) Fields .x, .y, .plane (read-only) Offset t:derive(dx, dy[, dplane]) → WorldTile Distance t:distanceTo(other[, alg]) → number — alg: "chebyshev" (default), "manhattan", "euclidean" In range t:withinRange(other, r) → bool — Chebyshev, plane-aware Jitter t:randomize(rx, ry) → WorldTile — random tile in the ±rx × ±ry box (humanized target) Compare t:equals(other) → bool (also the == operator)

Chebyshev distance matches OSRS 8-way walk distance.

docs.title: WorldArea
docs.text:
A rectangle or circle on one plane — pure value math (no engine reads), so it's valid off-tick and usable as an argument across the API. Construct via srs.area.rect / srs.area.circle (above).

Method Lua Notes Contains a:contains(tile) / a:contains(x, y) → bool plane-aware for the tile form Center a:center() → WorldTile Random tile a:randomTile() → WorldTile uniform inside the shape Overlap a:overlaps(other) → bool bounding-box: exact rect-rect, conservative for circles Size a:width(), a:height() → int Field a.plane (read-only) 
-- Guard a mining spot and pick a humanized stand tile.
local rocks = srs.area.rect(3280, 3365, 3288, 3372)
if not rocks:contains(srs.player.position()) then
    local t = rocks:randomTile()
    srs.walk.to(t.x, t.y, t.plane)      -- srs.walk.to takes numbers, not a tile
end

local home = WorldTile.new(3222, 3218)
if srs.player.position():distanceTo(home) > 20 then
    local t = home:randomize(1, 1)      -- don't click the exact same pixel every time
    srs.walk.to(t.x, t.y, t.plane)
end

docs.title: Bank
docs.text:
srs.bank

Full bank workflow: navigation to named banks, opening / closing, tab switching, per-item withdraw + deposit, bulk deposit, scrolling, and the "1 / 5 / 10 / X / All" quantity preset.

docs.title: Bank PIN
docs.text:
Auto-enter the bound account's 4-digit PIN on the keypad. The PIN itself is stored in the launcher's per-account encrypted record (DPAPI, user-scope) and never crosses the script API boundary — handleBankPin takes no PIN argument and hasBoundBankPin only exposes a boolean. The client reads the PIN only for the instant it needs one digit, clicks that digit's button on the keypad (group 213), and wipes it again before returning.

Method Lua Auto-enter the PIN srs.bank.handleBankPin() → bool Has a PIN been bound srs.bank.hasBoundBankPin() → bool

Per-call flow (at most one keypad click per call):

  1. Bail with true (no-op success) if the PIN widget isn't open.
  2. Bail with false if no account is bound, the account has no PIN, or the keypad's digit labels haven't been populated yet (the engine's CS2 script that writes them runs on the next engine tick after the keypad opens — see "Why tick-driven" below).
  3. Read widget (213, 10) to determine which digit position the keypad is currently asking for (FIRST / SECOND / THIRD / FOURTH). Bail with false if the text doesn't match yet (engine mid-update).
  4. Read the digit for the current position and scan the keypad letter slots' dynamic children for one whose text matches.
  5. Move the cursor onto that digit and click it like a player would (press, a short human-length hold, release). The game's own click handling records the digit and advances the instruction text. If the digit's label is blank because the cursor is hovering its button (the keypad hides the label under the cursor), the digit is inferred by elimination from the other nine.
  6. Wipe the PIN from memory.

While a click is settling (up to ~1.2 s, until the instruction moves on to the next digit) further calls return true without clicking again, so calling every pulse never enters a digit twice.

Why tick-driven: the game writes the keypad's (shuffled) digit labels a frame or two after the keypad appears, so they are empty on the first call. Rather than block waiting for them, each call returns in <1 ms (false until the labels are populated) and the script re-polls until the keypad closes.

Why a real click: the keypad only records a digit when its button's own click handler runs. Clicking the button the way a player does lets the game run that handler itself, so there is nothing build-specific to keep in sync.

Return values:

  • true — PIN widget isn't open (no-op), a click was dispatched, or the previous click is still settling this tick.
  • false — no account bound, account has no PIN, keypad labels aren't populated yet, instruction text doesn't match a known phrase, the digit widget can't be found in group 213, or the click couldn't be sent (game window input not hooked yet).

Calling pattern — call every pulse while the PIN widget is open:

script.pulse(function()
  if srs.bank.isPinOpen() then
    if not srs.bank.hasBoundBankPin() then
      log.info("Bind an account with a PIN via the launcher Accounts panel")
      return
    end
    srs.bank.handleBankPin()
  end
end)

To set a PIN for an account, open the launcher's Accounts modal, enter a 4-digit PIN in the "Bank PIN" field, and save. The PIN is encrypted alongside the password and only the bound game tab can read it back (DPAPI user-scope + per-binary entropy salt).

BankInfo (the table returned by srs.bank.info):

Field Type Notes x / y / plane integer Bank booth-row tile displayName string Human-readable location name

docs.text:
Method Lua Open via nearest banker srs.bank.open() → bool Close (X-button) srs.bank.close() → bool

open matches bankers by name list (Banker / Banker Tutor / Sigli the Huntsman / Astley / Felkrash) and interacts with the nearest match. Returns false if no banker is in scene.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The bank has 10 tabs: 0 = "All Items" (∞ icon), 1..9 = user-configurable. Current tab lives in varbit BANK_CURRENTTAB (4150). Most scrolling / per-item flows operate on the All Items view — srs.bank.scrollToSlot switches to it (and asks you to call again) if you're on another tab.

Method Lua Current tab srs.bank.currentTab() → int Open a specific tab srs.bank.openTab(idx) → bool Open All Items (∞) srs.bank.openMainTab() → bool

Tab clicks are dispatched against the tab row of the bank interface. The call returns false if the bank isn't open or the index is out of range.

docs.title: Container reads
docs.text:
Method Lua All slots srs.bank.all() → table (1-based list of items) Contains by id srs.bank.contains(id) → bool Contains by name srs.bank.contains(name) → bool Count by id srs.bank.count(id) → int Count by name srs.bank.count(name) → int

Name lookups match the item's in-game display name (case- and whitespace-insensitive substring). contains("prayer potion") matches all 4 dose variants because every dose string contains it.

Bank slot index

The slot field on items returned from srs.bank.all() is the bank container index (0..hundreds), not a backpack 0..27 index. The container is laid out in tab order — slots [0..N1-1] for tab 1, then [N1..N1+N2-1] for tab 2, ..., then untabbed (tab 0) at the end. The "All Items" visual view renders untabbed FIRST with partial-row breaks between sections — scrollToSlot does the visual-row math for you.

docs.title: Closed-bank cache
docs.text:
The live all/contains/count reads above only work while the bank UI is open — the engine drops the container the moment it closes, so count returns 0 from anywhere else. For routing and restock decisions ("do I have teleport runes stashed before I walk to a bank?") the host keeps a best-effort snapshot, refreshed every tick the bank is open, that persists after it closes.

Method Lua Notes Ever snapshotted? srs.bank.cachedPopulated() → bool false until the bank has been opened once this session Cached count srs.bank.cachedCount(id) → int last-known bank quantity of id (0 if absent/never seen) Cached has srs.bank.cachedHas(id [, min]) → bool cachedCount(id) >= min (default min = 1) Cached contents srs.bank.cachedContents() → table full { [itemId] = quantity } snapshot copy

Best-effort — may be stale

The snapshot reflects the last time the bank was open on this client. Banking on another client, or spending from the bank elsewhere, won't be reflected. Treat it as a planning hint, not ground truth — re-open the bank (isOpen() + the live reads) before acting on an exact quantity.

-- Decide whether to restock without walking to a bank first.
if srs.bank.cachedPopulated() and not srs.bank.cachedHas(561, 100) then   -- nature runes
    log.info("low on nature runes in the bank — buy more")
end
for id, qty in pairs(srs.bank.cachedContents()) do
    -- e.g. tally stashed supplies
end

docs.text:
Method Lua Scroll a slot into view srs.bank.scrollToSlot(slot) → bool Mouse-wheel notches srs.bank.scrollWheel(n) → bool Raw widget scrollY read srs.widget.scrollY(g, c) → int or nil Raw widget scrollY write srs.widget.setScrollY(g, c, y) → bool

scrollToSlot is the high-level helper: it computes the visual row accounting for tab partial-row breaks, and drives both the scroll value and the scrollbar redraw so the list actually moves. Returns true if the row is already in view (no-op). If the bank isn't on the All Items tab it fires the tab switch and returns false — call it again next tick.

scrollWheel synthesizes WM_MOUSEWHEEL events over the bank center — positive notches scroll DOWN, negative UP. Blocks ~16 ms per notch.

docs.title: Per-item withdraw
docs.text:
All variants click the bank item at widget (12, 12) (the bank's item grid), using the item's slot in the bank container and the menu op for the requested quantity. The caller picks the item by id or by name (case-insensitive partial match).

Method Lua Withdraw 1 srs.bank.withdrawOne(id\|name) → bool Withdraw N srs.bank.withdrawX(id\|name, amount) → bool Withdraw all srs.bank.withdrawAll(id\|name) → bool Withdraw all-but-one srs.bank.withdrawAllButOne(id\|name) → bool

Identifier mapping: - 2 = Withdraw-1, 3 = Withdraw-5, 4 = Withdraw-10 - 7 = Withdraw-All, 8 = Withdraw-All-but-1

withdrawX amount semantics: - {1, 5, 10} → single packet via fixed identifier (instant) - Any other amount → opens the Withdraw-X prompt (identifier 6), waits for the "Enter amount" chatbox input (up to ~2.4 s), then types each digit and presses Enter. Blocks roughly 1-3 seconds.

Placeholders (id present, quantity 0) are skipped — every withdraw finds the first slot with a positive quantity. Withdraws return false when the inventory is full, except withdrawAllButOne, which returns true in that case.

docs.title: Per-item deposit
docs.text:
The deposit-side inventory inside the bank window is widget (15, 3) (the backpack shown beside the bank). Clicks target that widget with the backpack slot (0..27) and the item id in that slot. The deposit-side op ordering differs from the withdraw side: explicit Deposit-1 / 5 / 10 / X / All ops (identifiers 3 / 4 / 5 / 7 / 8).

Method Lua Deposit all except (by id) srs.bank.depositAllExcept({ids...}) → bool Deposit all except (by name) srs.bank.depositAllExcept({"names"...}) → bool Deposit item / N srs.bank.deposit(id\|name, amount) → bool Deposit whole stack srs.bank.depositAll(id\|name) → bool

deposit uses the explicit Deposit-1 / 5 / 10 ops for those amounts and Deposit-X (the server-driven chatbox prompt, via srs.prompt) for any other amount — so it blocks while typing a custom amount. depositAll uses the explicit Deposit-All op for the whole stack. Because every click uses its own explicit op rather than the quantity preset's default, deposits are independent of the bank's current quantity setting (setWithdrawQuantity only affects withdraws).

depositAllExcept fires Deposit-All on the FIRST non-kept inventory slot per call and returns false; the script polls each tick until only kept items remain, at which point it returns true.

docs.title: Potion storage
docs.text:
Method Lua Panel showing srs.bank.potionStore.isOpen() → bool Open / close panel srs.bank.potionStore.open() / close() → bool Withdraw n potions srs.bank.potionStore.withdraw(idOrName, n) → bool Withdraw all / all but one srs.bank.potionStore.withdrawAll(idOrName) / withdrawAllButOne(idOrName) Set dose size (1..4) srs.bank.potionStore.setWithdrawDoses(idOrName, doses) → bool Current dose size srs.bank.potionStore.getWithdrawDoses(idOrName) → int (0 = not stored / not loaded) Deposit n / all srs.bank.potionStore.deposit(idOrName, n) / depositAll(idOrName) Contents loaded srs.bank.potionStore.isLoaded() → bool Stored potions srs.bank.potionStore.all() → list of StoredPotion Doses of a potion srs.bank.potionStore.doses(idOrName) → int Potions at current dose size srs.bank.potionStore.count(idOrName) → int Has at least one potion srs.bank.potionStore.contains(idOrName) → bool Empty vials srs.bank.potionStore.vials() → int

Reads work with the bank closed. Contents come from the game's own potion-store scripts and are cached until a potion-store varp changes; the first call after inject returns an empty list until isLoaded() is true (usually within a tick).

StoredPotion fields: enumId, name (no dose suffix, e.g. "Prayer potion"), itemId (item withdrawn at the current dose size), doses (total), withdrawDoses (1..4), count (doses / withdrawDoses), unfinished (unfinished potions and herb vials). doses(id) matches any of the potion's 1..4-dose item ids; doses(name) sums every potion whose name contains it. count and contains match the same way but count whole potions at the store's current withdraw size, so count(x) lines up with withdraw(x, n); leftover doses below that size don't make contains true.

srs.bank.contains / count / all cover the bank only — potion storage is never included. To check both:

local ps = srs.bank.potionStore
if srs.bank.contains("Prayer potion") or ps.contains("Prayer potion") then ... end

Withdraw and deposit need the bank open and the potion storage panel open (open() first). withdraw amounts are potions at the store's current dose size for that potion (withdrawDoses), which setWithdrawDoses(x, 1..4) changes — it's per potion, saved by the game, and shows in withdrawDoses a tick or so later. It always clicks, since the size the client has cached can lag the server; wait for getWithdrawDoses to read the new size before withdrawing. 1/5/10 use fixed ops, any other amount goes through Withdraw-X and blocks while it types. Withdraw by name matches the first stored potion whose name contains the text. The panel scrolls to the potion on its own. Deposits use the bank's normal Deposit ops — with the panel open the game puts potions into the store; the functions refuse when the panel is shut, so a potion never lands in the bank by mistake.

if srs.bank.potionStore.isLoaded() then
  for _, p in ipairs(srs.bank.potionStore.all()) do
    print(p.name, p.doses, p.count .. " x (" .. p.withdrawDoses .. ")")
  end
end

docs.text:
Sticky across subsequent withdraw clicks. Mirrors the "1 / 5 / 10 / X / All" button row at the bottom of the bank UI.

Method Lua Set quantity srs.bank.setWithdrawQuantity(q) → bool
