The step-by-step path. Most scripts want buyItem / sellItem instead.

Method Lua Start a BUY on an empty box; opens setup + search srs.ge.createBuyOffer(slot) → bool Start a SELL on an empty box — [UNVERIFIED] srs.ge.createSellOffer(slot) → bool Pick a SELL item from the side inventory srs.ge.setOfferItem(invSlot, itemId) → bool Quantity +1 srs.ge.addQuantity1() → bool Quantity +10 srs.ge.addQuantity10() → bool Quantity +100 srs.ge.addQuantity100() → bool Quantity +All srs.ge.addQuantityAll() → bool Open the exact-quantity chatbox prompt srs.ge.promptQuantity() → bool Price −5% srs.ge.decreasePrice5pct() → bool Price −1% srs.ge.decreasePrice1pct() → bool Price +1% srs.ge.increasePrice1pct() → bool Price +5% srs.ge.increasePrice5pct() → bool Open the exact-price chatbox prompt srs.ge.promptPrice() → bool Confirm the offer being set up srs.ge.confirm() → bool

createSellOffer is [UNVERIFIED]

A SELL offer is begun by clicking the item in the GE side inventory (setOfferItem, group 467), not by an empty-box action. createSellOffer(slot) exists for API symmetry but fires an unverified box action which may be a no-op — sellItem does not use this path. Prefer sellItem / setOfferItem.

docs.title: Exact entry & search (blocking)
docs.text:
Method Lua Type an exact quantity into the prompt srs.ge.setQuantity(quantity) → bool Type an exact price into the prompt srs.ge.setPrice(price) → bool Type an item name into the buy-search box srs.ge.searchItem(itemName) → bool

These open the relevant chatbox prompt, type the value with human-paced timing, wait for the input queue to drain, and (for numbers) submit with Enter. searchItem populates the result list (shown as children of the chatbox search results component, 162/53) but does not pick a result — use buyItem for the full flow, which also selects the matching result.

docs.title: One-call offers (blocking)
docs.text:
The high-level surface — find a slot, select the item, set quantity + price, confirm, all in one call. The GE offer screen must already be open.

Method Lua Place a complete buy offer srs.ge.buyItem(itemId\|name, quantity, price) → bool Place a complete sell offer srs.ge.sellItem(itemId\|name, quantity, price) → bool

Both accept either an item id (number) or a display name (string) as the first argument. price is gp-per-item; pass <= 0 to leave the engine's default guide price untouched. quantity must be > 0. buyItem types the name into the search box and selects the match (the by-id form resolves the display name via the live item cache); sellItem requires the item in your backpack and picks its slot automatically. Returns true only if the flow ran through Confirm.

For sensible prices, pair these with the market-price helpers on the same srs.ge table — e.g. srs.ge.buyItem(id, qty, srs.ge.buyPrice(id)).

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
GeOfferInfo — one offer slot. Fields are read-only; the is* helpers are called with : (offer:isFinished()).

Field Type Meaning slot integer Slot index 0..7 (−1 if invalid) state srs.ge.State value Lifecycle (see below) itemId integer Traded item id (−1 if empty) totalQuantity integer Offer size quantityDone integer Bought / sold so far price integer Price per item on the offer spent integer gp moved so far

Helpers: isEmpty(), isActive(), isComplete(), isFinished().

GeState (Lua srs.ge.State.* — there is no global GeState):

Const Value Meaning Empty 0 Slot unused CancelledBuy 1 Buy aborted CancelledSell 2 Sell aborted Buying 3 Active buy Bought 4 Buy complete Selling 5 Active sell Sold 6 Sell complete

Terminal states are best-effort

Empty / Buying / Selling are read directly from the live offers. The terminal bytes (Bought / Sold, and the cancelled split) are best-effort decodes — gate on isFinished() / anyFinished() rather than a specific terminal value where you can.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Buy 1000 nature runes at the instant-buy price, then collect when done.
local NATURE = 561
script.onTick(function()
    if not srs.ge.isOpen() then return end          -- open via the clerk first
    if srs.ge.slotOf(NATURE) < 0 and srs.ge.firstEmptySlot() >= 0 then
        srs.ge.buyItem(NATURE, 1000, srs.ge.buyPrice(NATURE))
    elseif srs.ge.anyFinished() then
        srs.ge.collectToInventory()
    end
end)

docs.title: GraphicsObjects
docs.text:
srs.graphicsObjects

Read-only enumeration of tile-bound SpotAnims — falling debris during boss fights, acid pools (Vasa, Tekton), blood splatters, spell-impact tile effects, teleport sparkles, run-energy regen sparkles, and so on.

Experimental — only id is verified

The engine's graphics-object list is bound automatically at startup, so the query methods work without setup. Only id is verified on the current client build; the remaining fields are unverified and may read as placeholder values. If a client update breaks the binding, the queries read empty — use scan() / setContainerOffset() (see Setup) to re-point it.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua All live gfx objects srs.graphicsObjects.all() → table[] Filter by tile window srs.graphicsObjects.nearby(cx, cz, plane, radius) → table[] Earliest-started entry (lowest startCycle) srs.graphicsObjects.next() → table \| nil

nearby(cx, cz, plane, radius) returns entries whose tileX/tileZ are within Chebyshev distance radius of (cx, cz) on the given plane.

next() returns the active graphics object with the lowest startCycle — the one that began rendering first — or nil when none are active. It is a best-effort proxy for "ends first": the engine exposes no end time, since duration comes from the animation definition.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Helpers for re-pointing the query if the automatic binding stops working on a new client build (see the warning above). Most scripts never need these.

Method Lua Probe candidate offsets srs.graphicsObjects.scan(base?) → table[] Pin the container offset srs.graphicsObjects.setContainerOffset(offset, base?) → bool Read the current offset srs.graphicsObjects.containerOffset() → integer Read the current base srs.graphicsObjects.containerBase() → integer

scan probes each world instance (base = 0) or its scene (base = 1) looking for a list shaped like the gfx-object container, returning one row per candidate. Pick the plausible row and pass its offset / base to setContainerOffset; the choice is session-persistent.

GraphicsObjectScanRow:

Field Type Notes offset integer Base-relative offset probed base integer 0 = world instance, 1 = scene entriesFound integer Plausible entries at that offset shapeOk boolean Begin/end looked like a sorted-set idsLookValid boolean Entries had plausible spotanim ids firstId integer A sample id, to recognize the effect

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Each entry is a plain table:

Field Type Notes id integer SpotAnim cache id. animationId integer The bound animation id (resolved from the spotanim's animation definition). Negative until the engine binds the animation. plane integer 0..3 tileX integer World tile X. tileZ integer World tile Y (Z in our naming). fineX integer Engine sub-tile coordinate (localTileX * 128 + 64). fineY integer Engine sub-tile coordinate. height integer Height value relative to the tile. startCycle integer The engine cycle at which this gfx began (or will begin) rendering. The gfx is in a "pending" state until currentCycle >= startCycle, then plays for the duration baked into its animation definition. framesSinceStart integer currentFrame - startCycle. Negative while pending, positive while rendering. Not a lifetime countdown — the actual end is determined by the animation's own length. finished boolean true once the engine has released the bound animation (the gfx is done playing and will be pruned on the next engine tick).

docs.title: List active gfx near the player
docs.text:
local p = srs.player.position()
for _, g in ipairs(srs.graphicsObjects.nearby(p.x, p.y, p.plane, 5)) do
    log.info(string.format("gfx id=%d at (%d, %d)", g.id, g.tileX, g.tileZ))
end

docs.title: Dodge dangerous tiles
docs.text:
A boss-mechanic dodger. Maintains a set of "lethal" spotanim ids and walks the player off any tile currently flagged as dangerous.

-- Tune for the boss you're fighting.
local DANGEROUS_IDS = { [1448]=true, [1295]=true, [1259]=true }

script.onTick(function()
    -- Build the current dangerous-tile list from live gfx.
    local danger = {}
    for _, g in ipairs(srs.graphicsObjects.all()) do
        if DANGEROUS_IDS[g.id] and not g.finished then
            danger[#danger+1] = { x=g.tileX, y=g.tileZ, plane=g.plane }
        end
    end
    if #danger == 0 then return end

    local p = srs.player.position()
    local onDanger = false
    for _, d in ipairs(danger) do
        if d.plane==p.plane and d.x==p.x and d.y==p.y then
            onDanger = true; break
        end
    end
    if not onDanger then return end

    -- Find the closest walkable safe tile and walk there.
    local safe = game.findSafeTile(p.x, p.y, danger, 5)
    if safe then
        game.walkSmart(safe.x, safe.y, safe.plane)
        log.info(string.format("Dodging to (%d, %d)", safe.x, safe.y))
    end
end)

See Walk for findSafeTile / walkSmart / walkFastCanvas documentation. Note game.findSafeTile (used above) lives on the global game table.

docs.title: React to a specific cast
docs.text:
Wait until a particular spotanim id appears and react once it's been rendering for a few frames.

local TARGET_ID = 1042   -- replace with the id you care about

script.onTick(function()
    for _, g in ipairs(srs.graphicsObjects.all()) do
        if g.id == TARGET_ID and g.framesSinceStart >= 0 and not g.finished then
            -- gfx is currently rendering — react now
            log.info(string.format("Target gfx active at (%d, %d)", g.tileX, g.tileZ))
            return
        end
    end
end)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• framesSinceStart is NOT a "time until removal" countdown. The engine prunes the gfx based on the animation's natural length, not from a counter on the gfx-object itself. Use finished to detect end-of-life.
  • fineX/fineY vs tileX/tileZ. Both are exposed for convenience. tileX/tileZ give world tile coordinates; fineX/fineY give the engine's sub-tile units (tile * 128 + 64). For tile-equality comparisons against srs.player.position(), use tileX/tileZ.
  • Pending gfx. When a spotanim has a start-delay in its packet (chained / sequenced effects), it appears in the list with framesSinceStart < 0 before it actually starts rendering. Filter on framesSinceStart >= 0 if you only care about currently-visible effects.

docs.title: GroundItem
docs.text:
srs.grounditem

Read-only enumeration of dropped items in every loaded scene, all 4 planes. The nearest* finders and loot(id) / lootByName use Chebyshev tile distance from the local player.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua All ground items srs.grounditem.all() → table (1-based list) By id srs.grounditem.byId(id) → table By name srs.grounditem.byName(name) → table Nearest (any) srs.grounditem.nearest() → GroundItemEntry \| nil Nearest by id srs.grounditem.nearestById(id) → GroundItemEntry \| nil Nearest by name srs.grounditem.nearestByName(name) → GroundItemEntry \| nil Loot nearest pile of id srs.grounditem.loot(id) → bool Loot nearest pile by name srs.grounditem.lootByName(name) → bool Loot exactly this pile srs.grounditem.loot(entry) → bool Examine srs.grounditem.examine(entry) → bool

Name lookups match the item's in-game display name (case- and whitespace-insensitive substring). byName("bones") returns all bone variants on the floor.

loot / lootByName click the pile's first option (Take) through the always-on input spoof and the engine action dispatch. Returns false if no match, the tile isn't visible on screen, or the spoofer can't inject.

loot(id) / lootByName(name) ignore ownership

Both take the nearest matching pile (Chebyshev distance from you), whoever it belongs to. To loot only your own drops, pick an entry yourself (filter on isMine) and pass it to loot(entry).

loot(entry) loots exactly that pile. It re-reads the live scene and matches by item id + tile + plane + ownership (preferring the same quantity), so a stale entry never fires at a different player's pile on the same tile. Returns false if the pile is gone. loot accepts either an item id or a GroundItemEntry.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
GroundItemEntry (read-only):

Field Type Notes id integer Item id quantity integer tileX integer tileY integer plane integer ownership integer Server-reported owner class, see constants below isMine boolean true when the item counts as your loot (see below)

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Ownership values are sent by the server with every ground item:

Meaning Lua Value Map spawn / nobody srs.grounditem.Ownership.None 0 Dropped by or rewarded to you srs.grounditem.Ownership.Self 1 Another player srs.grounditem.Ownership.Other 2 Your ironman group srs.grounditem.Ownership.Group 3

Use isMine, not ownership == Self

On an account that is not a group ironman the server reports other players' drops as Group (both sides have group id -1). isMine is true for Self, and for Group only while the local account type is a group-ironman variant, so it is the right test for "loot my items only".

Note

Items you have not received an OBJ_ADD for — other players' drops before they become public — are not in the pile at all, so they never appear in all(). Ownership is fixed when the pile entry is created.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local bones = srs.grounditem.nearestByName("Bones")
if bones then
    if srs.grounditem.loot(bones.id) then
        log.info(("looting bones at %d, %d"):format(bones.tileX, bones.tileY))
    end
end

Loot only your own drops (ironman-safe) — pick the nearest isMine pile yourself, then loot exactly that one:

local me = srs.player.position()
local best, bestDist
for _, g in ipairs(srs.grounditem.byName("seed")) do
    if g.isMine and g.plane == me.plane then
        local d = math.max(math.abs(g.tileX - me.x), math.abs(g.tileY - me.y))
        if not bestDist or d < bestDist then best, bestDist = g, d end
    end
end
if best then srs.grounditem.loot(best) end

docs.title: Hit splats
docs.text:
srs.hitsplats

The engine's hit-splat feed — every damage number the server applies to any actor in the scene, with the victim resolved.

This is combat ground truth. The server tells the client "actor X took N damage of type T", and this API is that message, not an inference from animations or interaction state. Reach for it whenever a script needs to know that combat is actually happening:

Question Alternative Why hit splats win Am I actually attacking? player animation id (426 bow / 1167 staff) ids are build-specific and unverified; a missed tick looks identical to a miss-click Am I still in this fight? srs.player.idleTicks your block animation resets it every time the boss hits you, so it never goes idle Is this the right target? srs.combat.isInteractingWith — this one is now exact (Combat); it tells you what the client intends, while a splat is what actually landed Is my protection prayer right? — a zero-damage splat (blocked == true) is direct proof Did it die? HP bar polling the server only pushes an HP ratio for ~6s after a hit

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Splats in the last N ticks (any actor) srs.hitsplats.recent([ticks]) → table Splats that landed on you srs.hitsplats.onSelf([ticks]) → table Splats that landed on one entity srs.hitsplats.onTarget(target [, ticks]) → table Is the engine hook installed? srs.hitsplats.isActive() → bool Splats observed this session srs.hitsplats.totalSeen() → number Subscribe to splats srs.hitsplats.onApplied(fn) → token Unsubscribe srs.hitsplats.offApplied(token) → bool

ticks is a lookback window in game ticks; omit it (or pass 0) for "this tick only". Lists come back oldest-first. target is an ActionTarget from srs.npc.* / entity.*; it is matched by spawnIndex. onApplied(fn) takes a function that receives one entry table per splat; offApplied returns false for an unknown or already-removed token.

The first poll returns empty

The feed is idle-gated — it costs nothing until something wants it. Your first recent/onSelf/onTarget call arms it and returns an empty table; poll again on the next tick. It disarms again after ~10s with no reads and no subscribers.

docs.title: Entry shape
docs.text:
Every entry — from recent, the filtered reads, or onApplied — is a plain Lua table (target is the one field that differs, see below):

field type meaning hitType integer raw engine type id — branch on this type string decoded name: "corruption" (0), "poison" (2), "venom" (5), "block" (12), "damage" (16), "shield" (18), else "unknown". The decode is provisional — see below amount integer damage; 0 means blocked / miss blocked boolean amount == 0 soakType integer soak type id, -1 when absent soakAmount integer soaked damage tick integer game tick the splat was delivered on wallClock number Millisecond timestamp (system uptime clock, GetTickCount64) when the splat was applied isSelf boolean landed on the local player targetKind string "self" / "npc" / "player" / "unresolved" spawnIndex integer entity index, -1 when unresolved targetId integer NPC definition id (0 for players) targetName string display name, "" when unresolved tileX tileY plane integer victim's tile target ActionTarget | nil live target, so e.target:attack() works. Only set on entries from the polling reads (recent / onSelf / onTarget), and only for NPC victims still in the scene; nil for "self" and "player" splats, for despawned victims, and always nil in onApplied events

target is nil once the victim has despawned (a kill, or the splat that killed it), and is never present on onApplied events — the flat targetId / targetName / spawnIndex fields are always present, so a splat is never dropped just because its actor is gone. To act on the victim from an event, find it by spawnIndex / targetId (for example with srs.npc.byId).

NPC and player splats are attributed by different routes internally, but either way you get a spawnIndex — so an "unresolved" splat still tells you which actor was hit, even when its name or id could not be filled in.

Which hitType ids are supported

12 (block) and 16 (damage) are supported and cover ordinary combat. Every other id is passed through as the raw number, and type reads "unknown" when an id has no name. Branch on the numeric hitType, not on type, for anything outside block and damage.

soakType / soakAmount are not supported

These two are exposed on the entry but carry no meaningful value today. Do not branch on them. amount and blocked are unaffected and reliable.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text: Nothing here runs Lua on the game thread: the engine hook queues, and the host drains + resolves splats on the script worker once per frame. So srs.hitsplats.onApplied fires on the script thread, exactly like srs.projectiles.onSpawned.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Confirm you are actually damaging the boss, rather than guessing from animations:

local boss = srs.npc.byName("Crystalline Hunllef")[1]
if boss then
    local hits = srs.hitsplats.onTarget(boss, 6)   -- last 6 ticks
    if #hits == 0 then
        log.info("not landing anything — re-clicking attack")
        boss:attack()
    end
end

Verify a protection prayer is on the right style:

for _, e in ipairs(srs.hitsplats.onSelf(4)) do
    if e.blocked then
        log.info("blocked a hit — prayer is correct")
    else
        log.info(("took %d (type %d) — wrong prayer?"):format(e.amount, e.hitType))
    end
end

Event form, with the per-kill bookkeeping a polling loop would miss:

local token = srs.hitsplats.onApplied(function(e)
    if e.isSelf then
        log.info(("me: %d (%s)"):format(e.amount, e.type))
    elseif e.targetName ~= "" then
        log.info(("%s: %d"):format(e.targetName, e.amount))
    end
end)
-- srs.hitsplats.offApplied(token)

Related

srs.events.on("hitsplat", fn) carries a cut-down version of the same feed (hitType, amount, soakType, and a numeric targetKind) through the central event registry. Use srs.hitsplats when you want the resolved target, the tick, or the polling reads.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
srs.input

Keyboard primitives. Two families live here, and they take different roads into the engine:

Family Road Reaches typeString, pressKey, pressEnter, pressEscape the engine's own InputEventManager (the keyPressed / keyChar / keyReleased trio a real key press posts), marshalled onto the render thread in-game text fields (chatbox prompts, GE search, display-name box, public chat) and the engine's keybinds keyTap / osKeyTap / isKeyPending raw WM_KEYDOWN / WM_KEYUP to the game's window procedure camera / movement keys held for a duration

Both are per-window and focus-independent: they work while the client is backgrounded and with several clients running. Nothing here uses SendInput.

The WndProc road does not type text in-game

Since build 238.5 the engine gates the synthetic WM_CHAR path to real OS input, so a WndProc keystroke never lands in an in-game text field. Use typeString / pressEnter for anything with a text box, and keep keyTap for what it was built for: holding arrow keys for the camera.

Not on the login screen

The engine-queue road feeds the logged-in input pipeline only. On the title / login screen typeString and pressKey do nothing; credential entry is handled inside the break manager and is deliberately not reachable from scripts.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Lua Type text into the focused field (blocks) srs.input.typeString(text) → int Type, then Enter (blocks) srs.input.typeString(text, submit) → int Type with a custom pacing band (blocks) srs.input.typeString(text, submit, minMs, maxMs) → int Tap one key, engine road (fire-and-forget) srs.input.pressKey(vk) → bool Enter, engine road srs.input.pressEnter() → bool Escape, engine road srs.input.pressEscape() → bool Tap a key, WndProc road srs.input.keyTap(vk, holdMs) Tap a key (deprecated alias of keyTap) srs.input.osKeyTap(vk, holdMs) Any WndProc release still scheduled? srs.input.isKeyPending() → bool

docs.title: typeString
docs.text:
Types text into whatever engine text field currently has keyboard focus. It opens and focuses nothing: fire the thing that opens the field first (a Withdraw-X click, a door, an NPC line), wait for it to render, then type. Text typed while no field has focus is silently swallowed by the engine. For the chatbox prompt use srs.dialogue.enterText / enterAmount (or srs.prompt.*), which wait for the prompt before typing.

  • Pacing. The gap between characters is drawn per character from [minMs, maxMs], default 80–160 ms — a hand, not a metronome.
  • Blocking. The calling script sleeps until the whole string has drained and settled: roughly #text × 120 ms + 300 ms, plus 250 + 300 ms when submit is true. Call it from pulse / onTick, never from draw, and call it once per field — not every tick.
  • Return value is the number of characters queued. Characters with no Windows virtual-key mapping (most non-ASCII) are skipped; the count tells you. With submit = true the Enter is sent even when the count is 0.
  • Case and shifted symbols come through verbatim: the character event carries the literal character.

docs.title: pressKey / pressEnter / pressEscape
docs.text: One non-character key through the engine road. vk is a Win32 virtual-key (0x0D Enter, 0x1B Escape, 0x09 Tab, 0x08 Backspace, 0x20 Space, digits and letters). Fire-and-forget: true means dispatched, not that the field reacted. pressEscape is the way to dismiss a chatbox prompt a script does not want to answer; pressEnter submits a field you typed into without submit.

docs.title: keyTap vs osKeyTap
docs.text: There is one WndProc path: keyTap posts WM_KEYDOWN now and schedules the WM_KEYUP for holdMs later (holdMs < 0 clamps to 0). The release fires every rendered frame (~16 ms granularity). osKeyTap is a deprecated alias that forwards to keyTap — it no longer uses SendInput and has no foreground requirement; it is kept only so older scripts keep working.

docs.title: VK constants
docs.text:
srs.input.VK.*:

Name Value VK LEFT 0x25 VK_LEFT UP 0x26 VK_UP RIGHT 0x27 VK_RIGHT DOWN 0x28 VK_DOWN SPACE 0x20 VK_SPACE ENTER 0x0D VK_RETURN ESCAPE 0x1B VK_ESCAPE TAB 0x09 VK_TAB BACKSPACE 0x08 VK_BACK

For other keys pass the raw VK integer (see Microsoft's Virtual-Key Codes).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
-- Tutorial Island display-name box (widget 558): focus it, type, then
-- press the "Set name" button. Once — not every tick.
if srs.widget.isOpen(558) and not typedName then
    srs.widget.clickReal(558, 7)              -- the NAME box
    local n = srs.input.typeString("kebab" .. math.random(100, 999))
    typedName = n > 0
    srs.widget.click(558, 19, "Set name")
end

-- Public chat: type and send in one call.
srs.input.typeString("gz", true)

-- Calibrate yaw-rotation rate (WndProc road): hold left arrow for 1s.
local y0 = srs.camera.getYaw()
srs.input.keyTap(srs.input.VK.LEFT, 1000)
script.nextTick(function()
    local y1 = srs.camera.getYaw()
    log.info(("Δyaw over 1s = %d units"):format((y1 - y0) % 2048))
end)

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text:
srs.inventory

Read-only view of the player's backpack (28 slots) plus item-action helpers.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Snapshot all slots srs.inventory.all() → table (1-based list) One slot (0..27) srs.inventory.at(slot) → InventoryItem \| nil Contains by id srs.inventory.contains(id) → boolean Contains by name srs.inventory.contains(name) → boolean Count by id srs.inventory.count(id) → integer Count by name srs.inventory.count(name) → integer First slot by id srs.inventory.firstSlot(id) → integer First slot by name srs.inventory.firstSlot(name) → integer Empty slots count srs.inventory.emptySlots() → integer Full srs.inventory.isFull() → boolean Empty srs.inventory.isEmpty() → boolean

Name lookups match the item's in-game display name (case- and whitespace-insensitive substring). contains("prayer potion") matches all 4 dose variants. firstSlot returns -1 if the item isn't present.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Method Lua Click action on slot or item name srs.inventory.interact(slot\|name, action) → boolean Click by id srs.inventory.interactById(id, action) → boolean Click by name srs.inventory.interactByName(name, action) → boolean Click lowest dose of a potion family srs.inventory.interactByLowestDose(baseName, action) → boolean Examine slot's item srs.inventory.examine(slot) → boolean Drop all by id srs.inventory.dropAll(id) → integer Drop all by name srs.inventory.dropAll(name) → integer Drops still queued srs.inventory.pendingDropCount() → integer Empty coal bag srs.inventory.emptyCoalBag() → boolean

action is the menu-option string (e.g. "Eat", "Drop", "Wield", "Bury", "Drink", "Use"). Returns false on any of: slot out of range, slot empty, slot widget not currently rendered, or spoofer failure. Any option the item lists in its inventory menu works, including item-specific verbs ("Lay", "Release", "Teleport", "Rub", …). A common verb (Eat, Drop, Wield, …) that this item doesn't list does not fail — it falls back to the item's primary (first) option — while an uncommon verb the item doesn't list returns false. Either way, spell the verb as the item's menu shows it.

interact takes either a slot (a number, 0–27) or an item name (a string: first slot whose item name contains it, case-insensitive — identical to interactByName). A number is always a slot, never an item id: to act on an item id use interactById.

srs.inventory.interact(0, "Drop")           -- slot 0
srs.inventory.interact("Lobster", "Eat")    -- first slot whose name contains "Lobster"
srs.inventory.interactById(379, "Eat")      -- by item id

interactByLowestDose targets the lowest dose of a potion family — interactByLowestDose("Prayer potion", "Drink") drinks a (1) before a fresh (4) to free inventory slots sooner (the trailing (N) is stripped from baseName).

examine fires the item's right-click Examine and the engine prints the description to chat (info-only, no server cost).

emptyCoalBag empties a coal bag via its contextual "Empty" op on the main inventory. Returns false if no coal bag is held. The fill half lives on the bank facade — srs.bank.fillCoalBag (bank must be open).

dropAll is asynchronous — poll pendingDropCount

dropAll returns the number of drops it queued and schedules them with human-like spacing (~50–200 ms apart plus a slot-distance term), so a full 28-slot drop plays out over several seconds. Do not call dropAll again each tick to "keep dropping" — that re-queues the whole set. Fire it once, then treat the drop as finished when pendingDropCount() returns 0.

docs.title: Use item on…
docs.text:
Stage an inventory item, then apply it to a target. Each takes either ids or a (srcSlot, entry) overload where entry is the finder result from the matching module.

Method Lua …on object srs.inventory.useItemOnObject(itemId, objectId) → boolean …on object (slot + entry) srs.inventory.useItemOnObject(srcSlot, entry) → boolean …on item srs.inventory.useItemOnItem(srcId, dstId) → boolean …on item, burst mode srs.inventory.useItemOnItemBatch(srcId, dstId, count) → boolean …on NPC srs.inventory.useItemOnNpc(itemId, npcId) → boolean …on NPC (slot + target) srs.inventory.useItemOnNpc(srcSlot, target) → boolean …on ground item srs.inventory.useItemOnGroundItem(itemId, groundItemId) → boolean …on ground item (slot + entry) srs.inventory.useItemOnGroundItem(srcSlot, entry) → boolean

useItemOnItem picks the first inventory slot holding each id (returns false if both resolve to the same slot). useItemOnItemBatch repeats the item-on-item up to count ∈ [1, 8] times for fast-fletching-style bursts.

NPC and ground-item variants not yet verified in game

useItemOnNpc and useItemOnGroundItem are bound and their menu actions follow the game's use-on-NPC / use-on-ground-item options, but they have not been tested against a live client. useItemOnObject and useItemOnItem are the established paths. Test on a harmless target before depending on them.

How the use-on calls behave

Every useItemOn* call is two clicks: it stages the inventory item ("Use") immediately and fires the click on the target 150–300 ms later. true means the stage click was queued, not that the target click landed — the completion bails (logged to the console) if the target despawned, moved off-screen, or the staged item changed in the meantime. useItemOnNpc takes the target the srs.npc.* finders return and re-resolves it live at fire time; useItemOnGroundItem checks the pile is still on its tile first. Keep the target on screen (see srs.camera.ensureVisible).

docs.title: Constants
docs.text: The backpack holds 28 slots (indices 0..27); there is no Lua constant for it, so hardcode 28.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
InventoryItem (read-only):

Field Type Notes id integer OSRS item id; ≤ 0 means empty slot quantity integer Stack qty slot integer 0..27

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if srs.inventory.isFull() then
    srs.inventory.dropAll("Bones")
end
srs.inventory.interactByName("Lobster", "Eat")

docs.title: Magic
docs.text:
srs.magic

Cast spells using the Spells metadata table. All four spellbooks (Standard, Ancient, Lunar, Arceuus) share spellbook widget group 218; the matching book must be the active one when you cast.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Available rune count srs.magic.runeCount(runeItemId) → int Can cast (level + rune availability) srs.magic.canCast(s) → bool Cast (no-target / self) srs.magic.cast(s) → bool Two-click cast on inv slot srs.magic.castOnInventory(s, slot) → bool Two-click cast on an NPC srs.magic.castOnNpc(s, target) → bool Two-click cast on a ground item srs.magic.castOnGroundItem(s, entry) → bool Select the autocast spell srs.magic.setAutocast(s[, defensive]) → bool Autocast selected? srs.magic.isAutocasting() → bool Defensive autocast selected? srs.magic.isDefensiveAutocast() → bool Selected autocast spell srs.magic.autocastSpell() → int \| nil High alch convenience srs.magic.highAlch(slot) → bool Low alch convenience srs.magic.lowAlch(slot) → bool

canCast checks the Magic level plus every per-rune cost; runeCount totals the copies of one rune id. Both count inventory + rune pouch (the bank is never counted from Lua). Elemental-staff substitution is still TODO, so don't hard-gate a cast on canCast when the player wields a staff — try the cast and count failures instead.

cast fires the spell click — works for self-target / no-target spells (teleports, alchemy on self, etc.). It does not pre-select for use-on.

docs.title: Two-click casts
docs.text:
castOnInventory, castOnNpc and castOnGroundItem all drive the same engine state machine a player does: click the spell (stages it client-side, no packet), then click the target with the widget-target action for that target kind. The spell click fires immediately; the target click is scheduled 150–300 ms later on the engine queue, so the call returns true as soon as the spell click went out and the target click is queued. Poll the effect you care about (XP drop, inventory change, NPC animation, srs.combat.isInCombat()) rather than the return value.

  • castOnInventory(s, slot) — High Alchemy, Bones to Bananas, Superheat and other item-target spells (including the Arceuus reanimation spells, which target an ensouled head in the backpack).
  • castOnNpc(s, target) — target is what srs.npc.* / entity.* return. The NPC is re-resolved by spawn index right before the second click, so a snapshot from earlier in the tick is fine; the cast is dropped (with a console line) if it despawned or no longer projects on screen. Any in-flight walk is cancelled first, like srs.npc.interact. Wind Strike on a chicken, Stun / Bind / Snare / Entangle, Crumble Undead, Confuse / Weaken / Curse, the god spells, the Ancient combat spells, Monster Examine, the Arceuus Grasp / Demonbane spells and Dark Lure — see the per-book target tables in Spells. Player-target spells (Teleport Block, Cure Other, Stat Spy, Energy Transfer, Heal Other, Vengeance Other) are not supported by this call.
  • castOnGroundItem(s, entry) — entry from srs.grounditem.* (Telekinetic Grab). The pile must still be on that tile and on screen at fire time.

Self-cast Lunar and Arceuus spells (teleports, Vengeance, Spellbook Swap, ...) use plain cast.

All two-click casts (including highAlch / lowAlch) need the spellbook showing, and the script owns the tab: open it with srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.MAGIC) and check srs.tab.isOpen before casting. The API never switches tabs itself; when the book is not rendered it returns false and prints why. All variants return false when the spell metadata is unpopulated.

docs.title: Autocast
docs.text:
setAutocast(s[, defensive]) drives the combat tab, which the script opens first (srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.COMBAT); false when it is not showing): clicks the autocast button (593.28, or 593.23 for defensive), waits up to 1.5 s for the spell picker (group 201), clicks the matching entry (matched by label, then by icon sprite) and waits for varbit 276 to reflect the choice, retrying once with a real click. Returns true when varbit 276 shows s and the defensive-mode varbit (2668) matches defensive — including when they already did before the call. Autocast is supported for the 20 Standard strike → surge spells and the 16 Ancient combat spells (SMOKE_RUSH … ICE_BARRAGE); any other spell returns false. The game hides the autocast buttons unless a staff that can autocast the spell is wielded, so wield the staff first. The Lua call blocks the script for up to a few seconds while it waits.

autocastSpell() maps varbit 276 back to a srs.spell.* value (nil when nothing is set or the value is not one of the autocastable spells above); isAutocasting() is the cheap varbit ~= 0 check.

Not yet verified in game

castOnNpc, castOnGroundItem, the Ancient autocast entries and the autocast picker flow have not been fully tested in game. Planned checks: Wind Strike on a chicken, Telekinetic Grab on a dropped item, autocast Wind Strike with a staff of air, autocast Ice Barrage with an Ancient staff.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text: Spell and Spellbook constants live in Spells.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- castOnInventory / highAlch / lowAlch do not open the spellbook for you
if not srs.tab.isOpen(srs.tab.MAGIC) then srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.MAGIC) end
if srs.magic.canCast(srs.spell.HIGH_ALCHEMY) then
    srs.magic.highAlch(0)
end

-- Wind Strike on the nearest chicken (spellbook must be showing)
if not srs.tab.isOpen(srs.tab.MAGIC) then srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.MAGIC) end
local chicken = srs.npc.nearestByName("Chicken")
if chicken then srs.magic.castOnNpc(srs.spell.WIND_STRIKE, chicken) end

-- Telekinetic Grab a dropped item
local boot = srs.grounditem.nearestByName("Right boot")
if boot then srs.magic.castOnGroundItem(srs.spell.TELEKINETIC_GRAB, boot) end

-- Autocast Fire Strike (staff of air wielded), then attack
if srs.magic.autocastSpell() ~= srs.spell.FIRE_STRIKE then
    if srs.tab.isOpen(srs.tab.COMBAT) then
        srs.magic.setAutocast(srs.spell.FIRE_STRIKE)
    else
        srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.COMBAT)           -- the script owns the tab
    end
else
    local target = srs.npc.nearestByName("Chicken")
    if target then srs.npc.attack(target) end
end

docs.title: MenuEntry
docs.text:
srs.menuEntry / srs.menu

Typed fluent builder over the raw engine-action path. Goes through the same spoof-then-dispatch route as every other facade — fail-closed if the spoofer can't inject.

Use this when you need raw control over MenuAction params (for example to reproduce an interaction type the higher-level facades don't cover) without bypassing the input simulation contract.

The builder has no option/target text fields (those belong to the higher-level interaction path; this builder targets the raw MenuAction dispatch path).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local e = srs.menuEntry.new()
e:worldX(10):worldY(20)
 :opcode(srs.menuEntry.CC_OP)
 :screen(450, 300)
 :fire()

docs.title: Setters
docs.text:
Method Lua Set world X / slot entry:worldX(v) → entry Set world Y / widget id entry:worldY(v) → entry Encode a widget id entry:widget(g, c) → entry Set the opcode entry:opcode(op) → entry Set the spawn index entry:spawnIndex(v) → entry Set the subject value entry:subject(v) → entry Set the click pixel entry:screen(x, y) → entry Dispatch the action entry:fire() → bool

The factory is srs.menuEntry.new() → MenuEntry. Every setter returns the same entry, so calls chain.

docs.title: Field semantics
docs.text:
• worldX / worldY — primary param pair. For tile actions these are world tile coords; for inventory / widget actions, worldX is the slot/sub-id and worldY is the encoded widget id.
  • widget(g, c) — convenience that encodes (groupId, childId) into worldY = (group << 16) | child.
  • spawnIndex(v) — entity / loc spawn index for entity-targeted actions (NPC, object, ground item); leave 0 for widget and walk actions.
  • fire() — queues the action for the engine's main thread and returns true once queued (false when it cannot be queued).
  • subject(v) — extra unsigned subject value; leave 0 unless a capture of the action you are reproducing shows it set.
  • screen(x, y) — required. Pixel coords of the click target. The spoofer needs these to draw a plausible mouse trail. Sentinel (0, 0) causes the spoofer to skip and fail-closed.

docs.title: Opcode constants
docs.text:
srs.menuEntry.*:

Lua const Value Meaning WALK 23 Walk to a tile GROUND_ITEM_FIRST_OPTION 20 First option on a ground item (Take) ITEM_USE 25 Use an item CC_OP 57 Most widget / inventory actions WIDGET_USE_ON_WIDGET 58 Second click of "Use" CC_OP_LOW_PRIORITY 1007 Drop, Examine

docs.title: Reading the menu (srs.menu)
docs.text:
srs.menu is the reader counterpart to the builder above — it snapshots the engine's live menu-entry buffer.

Method Lua Entry count srs.menu.count() → int All entries srs.menu.entries() → table[] Has an option srs.menu.contains(opt) → bool Index of option srs.menu.indexOf(opt) → int (-1 if absent)

Each entry of entries() is a table with the fields option, target (colored label, may be empty), opcode, identifier, param0 / param1, spawnIndex. contains / indexOf match option case-insensitively and trimmed.

Indexing. entries() is a normal 1-based Lua list, while indexOf returns a 0-based position (-1 if absent) — add 1 to index into entries().

Ordering. Index 0 is the bottom of the visual menu (always Cancel) and the last entry is the left-click default — the same indices as before the 241.1 client update, which changed how the engine stores the menu.

Field meaning by entry kind:

Entry kind opcode identifier param0 / param1 spawnIndex Cancel 1006 — -1 — Walk here 23 — -1 — Loc 3-6 (ops 1-4), 1001 (op 5), 1002 (Examine) loc type id scene-relative tile X / Y raw index Ground item 18-22 (ops 1-5), 1004 (Examine) item type id scene-relative tile X / Y raw index NPC 9-13 (ops 1-5), 1003 (Examine) NPC index -1 NPC index Player 44-51 (ops 1-8; +2000 if deprioritised) player index -1 player index Widget 57 (ops 1-5) or 1007 (ops 6+) 1-based op number slot / packed widget id slot

A +2000 on opcode marks a deprioritised player option (e.g. Trade, Follow) on a player entry — it does not mark the default entry; use the last-index rule above. opcode is 0 for entry kinds the reader doesn't recognise.

It reads the HUMAN cursor's menu, not the bot's

The buffer is rebuilt every frame from the cursor's world tile by the engine's hover pass. SafeRS interactions are dispatched as spoofed MenuActions / packets and never build a menu, so this reader does not show what the bot is about to click. You see entries when a real right-click context menu is open or the mouse is hovering an entity — making this a diagnostic / human-in-the-loop tool (e.g. confirming what options an entity exposes). Treat it as a diagnostic aid rather than a load-bearing input to your script's logic.

-- log the menu whenever you right-click something
local last = ""
script.draw(function()
    local es = srs.menu.entries()
    local sig = ""
    for _, e in ipairs(es) do sig = sig .. e.option .. "|" end
    if sig ~= last then
        last = sig
        for i, e in ipairs(es) do
            log.info(("[%d] %q -> %q (op=%d)"):format(i, e.option, e.target, e.opcode))
        end
    end
end)

docs.title: Notify
docs.text:
srs.notify

Push a custom notification to the launcher. It appears in the launcher's Notifications panel as a "Script notification" entry and, when the user has a Discord webhook set and the "Script notifications" kind enabled for Discord (on by default), is posted to that channel too. Use it for events only your script knows about: a kill-count milestone, "out of supplies, stopping", a rare event.

Delivery is fire-and-forget. Nothing is sent when the client runs without a launcher (solo mode).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Send a notification srs.notify(title, message?) → bool Send with options srs.notify(title, message?, opts?) → bool Send with options, no message srs.notify(title, opts) → bool

srs.notify is a plain function (not a table). The second argument is either the message string or the options table; if it is a string, an options table may follow as the third argument. The notification is tagged with the calling script's name, which is shown with the notification.

Returns true if the notification was queued for the launcher, false when no launcher is attached, the title is empty, or the source is rate limited.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
NotifyOptions (a table, all keys optional):

Field Type Default Notes highlight boolean false Pin as a highlighted entry in the panel (same treatment as a rare drop) color integer -1 Discord embed colour as 0xRRGGBB; -1 = default script colour

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• title is required and is cut to 256 bytes; message may be empty and is cut to 2000 bytes (Discord embed limits). Invalid UTF-8 is replaced.
  • Each source is rate limited: a burst of 5, then one every 10 seconds. Calls over the limit are dropped and return false.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
srs.notify("Out of supplies", "Stopping the script.")

-- Highlighted, custom colour
srs.notify("Pet drop!", "Got the pet after 312 kills.",
           { highlight = true, color = 0xFFD700 })

-- Title + options only
srs.notify("Level up", { highlight = true })

Don't call it in a tight loop

Over-limit calls are silently dropped. Notify on state changes (a milestone reached, a script stopping), not every tick.

docs.title: NPC
docs.text:
srs.npc

Find NPCs in the scene and act on them. The srs.npc table carries both the finders (which NPCs are nearby) and the actions (attack, talk-to, …) so scripts can stay in one table.

A target is identified by its spawn index + world coords. The finders return the ActionTarget usertype, and the action functions take one, so srs.npc.attack(npc) / npc:attack() work on whatever a finder handed you.

All interact / attack / talkTo / bank / examine calls route through Interact, which always spoofs mouse motion + click before engine action dispatch (no escape hatch).

docs.title: Finding NPCs
docs.text:
Method Lua All NPCs in scene srs.npc.all() → table By id srs.npc.byId(id) → table By name srs.npc.byName(name) → table Nearest (any) srs.npc.nearest() → ActionTarget \| nil Nearest by id srs.npc.nearestById(id) → ActionTarget \| nil Nearest by name srs.npc.nearestByName(name) → ActionTarget \| nil

byName / nearestByName normalize the name internally (case- and whitespace-insensitive), so pass the in-game name as shown ("Banker", "Grand Exchange Clerk"). The srs.npc finders are the recommended going-forward form.

Three equivalent finder surfaces

Lua exposes the same finders three times — all hit the same backend, so pick whichever reads best and don't mix them for "different" results:

Global npc.* srs.npc.* entity.* npc.all() srs.npc.all() entity.npcs() npc.byId(id) srs.npc.byId(id) entity.npcById(id) npc.byName(name) srs.npc.byName(name) entity.npcByName(name) npc.nearest() srs.npc.nearest() entity.nearestNpc() npc.nearestById(id) srs.npc.nearestById(id) — npc.nearestByName(name) srs.npc.nearestByName(name) —

All return ActionTarget (lists or single-or-nil). The global npc table is a plain alias kept for source compatibility.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Generic interact srs.npc.interact(target, action) → bool Option by position srs.npc.interactOp(target, op[, label]) → bool Attack srs.npc.attack(target) → bool Talk-to srs.npc.talkTo(target) → bool Bank (banker NPCs) srs.npc.bank(target) → bool Examine srs.npc.examine(target) → bool Still in world map srs.npc.isAlive(target) → bool Overhead prayer headicon srs.npc.overheadPrayer(target) → OverheadPrayer Overhead chat text srs.npc.overheadText(target) → string Spotanims (graphics) on the actor srs.npc.spotAnims(target) → table Has a spotanim id srs.npc.hasSpotAnim(target, id) → bool

action is the exact menu-option string the game shows ("Attack", "Talk-to", "Bank", "Pickpocket", "Trade", "Steal-from", …). interactOp presses option op (1..5) of the NPC's menu by position instead of by text; any other op returns false. Use it for multi-state NPCs whose current options live on a varbit-selected child type — the parent type the game reports has no options at all, so interact("Start-trial") can't find the text and falls back to option 1. label is only used in logs (Lua: optional, defaults to "op<N>"). Like examine, interactOp is not an ActionTarget method — call srs.npc.interactOp(npc, 3).

examine fires the right-click Examine and the engine prints the NPC's description to chat.

overheadPrayer reads the NPC's protection-prayer headicon (live override when set, else the NpcType definition). Returns OverheadPrayer.None when the NPC shows no prayer icon or has despawned; only prayer-archive (440) icons are reported. See Prayer for the OverheadPrayer enum values — it's a Lua global enum, not under srs.npc.

overheadText is the chat text drawn above the actor right now — NPC forced chat (an entling's "Short on top!", a Forester's shout) or a player's public chat — the same text the game draws over the head. Returns "" when nothing is shown, when the NPC has despawned, or when the text has expired (the engine clears it the tick its countdown reaches zero). Every finder result also carries an overheadText snapshot field plus overheadCycles (client ticks left before it clears); the method re-reads the live actor and is what to use when you hold an older target. Works for NPC and player targets.

spotAnims lists the graphics playing on the actor right now: spell impacts, teleport flashes, boss charge-up effects. These are separate from tile graphics (GraphicsObjects) and in-flight Projectiles. An actor can carry several at once, each in its own slot. Each entry has:

Field Notes slot 0–255. Slot 0 is the classic single "graphic" id Spotanim id. This client's cache id, the same id space as projectile/graphics-object id height Draw height offset startCycle Absolute client cycle (50 per second) the effect starts at delay Client cycles until it starts (0 once playing) active false while it is still waiting on its start delay

The game drops each entry when its animation finishes, so the list only holds effects that are playing or about to start. It is empty when there are none. hasSpotAnim(target, id) is true for a pending effect as well, which lets you react to a boss charge-up before it plays. Both work for NPC and player targets and always read the live actor.

local boss = srs.npc.nearestByName("Hunllef")
if boss then
    for _, g in ipairs(boss:spotAnims()) do
        print(("slot %d  id %d  active %s"):format(g.slot, g.id, tostring(g.active)))
    end
    -- boss:hasSpotAnim(id) is true from the moment the server queues it
end

docs.title: Spotanim events
docs.text:
Method Lua Subscribe srs.npc.onSpotAnim(fn[, filter]) → token Unsubscribe srs.npc.offSpotAnim(token) → bool

onSpotAnim fires once for every new spotanim the server puts on any NPC or player. It fires on the frame the update arrives, so you don't need to poll spotAnims(). That is when the effect is queued. If the server gave it a delay, it starts drawing delay client cycles later, so you can react before it is even on screen. Callbacks run on the script thread in the same per-frame pass as srs.hitsplats.onApplied, roughly 16 ms after the update arrives. Cleared slots are not reported.

The callback receives a table:

Field Notes id, slot, height As in spotAnims() delay Client cycles until it starts drawing (0 = right away) startCycle Absolute client cycle it starts at persist true if the game keeps it after its animation ends targetKind "npc", "player", "self" or "unresolved" isSelf true when it landed on you spawnIndex The actor's server index (−1 if unknown) npcId, name NPC id and name (npcId −1 for players) tileX, tileY, plane Where the actor stood wallClock Milliseconds timestamp target The live NPC ActionTarget (NPC targets only, else nil), so e.target:attack() works

filter is optional. Pass a spotanim id (a number), or a table with any of id, npcId, spawnIndex and kind ("npc", "player" or "self"). Every field you give must match. The registration follows the same pause rules as pulse/onTick, and a script reload drops it.

local CHARGE = 1234  -- the boss's charge-up spotanim id
local tok = srs.npc.onSpotAnim(function(e)
    print(("%s got spotanim %d, starts in %d cycles"):format(e.name, e.id, e.delay))
end, { npcId = BOSS_ID, id = CHARGE })
-- later: srs.npc.offSpotAnim(tok)

isAlive semantics

isAlive checks that the NPC is still present in the world. After an NPC dies it lingers a few ticks playing the death animation, then despawns — once that happens isAlive returns false. Currently does not treat HP-0-but-still-rendering as "dead"; callers that need that (loot timing, drop tracking) should poll currentHp via the NPCs panel column or entity.npcById(...).

docs.title: ActionTarget method-call shortcuts (Lua)
docs.text:
The ActionTarget usertype exposes these as methods (use :):

Method Lua Generic interact t:interact(action) → bool Attack t:attack() → bool Talk-to t:talkTo() → bool Bank t:bank() → bool Still in world map t:isAlive() → bool Overhead prayer headicon t:overheadPrayer() → OverheadPrayer Spotanims on the actor t:spotAnims() → table Has a spotanim id t:hasSpotAnim(id) → bool Handle still valid t:isValid() → bool

For example:

local npc = entity.nearestNpc()
if npc and npc:isAlive() then
    npc:attack()         -- == srs.npc.attack(npc)
    npc:talkTo()
    npc:bank()
    npc:interact("Pickpocket")
    npc:overheadPrayer() -- == srs.npc.overheadPrayer(npc)
    npc:spotAnims()      -- == srs.npc.spotAnims(npc)
    npc:hasSpotAnim(id)  -- == srs.npc.hasSpotAnim(npc, id)
end

examine has no usertype shortcut

examine is the one action not exposed as an ActionTarget method — there is no npc:examine(). Call srs.npc.examine(npc).

docs.title: Target fields
docs.text:
Finders return the ActionTarget usertype. Its fields are read-only:

Field Notes kind TargetKind enum (TargetKind.None / Npc / Player / Object / Tile) tileX, tileY, tileZ World tile coords plane 0..3 spawnIndex Server-assigned spawn index entityId Item/Loc/Npc id depending on kind name Display name currentHp, maxHp Live HP (−1 = unknown; boss HP scaling is approximate) interactTarget Index of the actor this one is interacting with, within the kind given by interactTargetKind; -1 when not interacting interactTargetKind Kind of that target: 0 none, 1 NPC (interactTarget = NPC spawnIndex), 2 player (= player spawnIndex), 3 world entity. Always check the kind before comparing interactTarget animationId Active anim id modelMagnitude Engine getXYZMag half-extent (0 = unknown) overheadText Overhead chat text drawn right now ("" = none). Snapshot — see srs.npc.overheadText overheadCycles Client ticks until overheadText clears (0 = none) orientation Facing angle 0–2047, clockwise from south: 0 = S, 512 = W, 1024 = N, 1536 = E; −1 = unknown combatLevel Combat level (−1 = unknown)

Defs

For static NPC definition data (size, menu actions, max HP) see srs.defs in Defs.

orientation / combatLevel semantics

Both fields are populated for NPCs and players. orientation is the actor's target facing: the angle the engine turns toward, so it changes the tick the server sets it and the rendered model catches up over the next few ticks. Compare against the four cardinals with a tolerance (e.g. north = math.abs(o - 1024) <= 256) rather than exact equality if the NPC may be mid-turn. combatLevel is -1 for NPCs that show no level on the right-click (bankers, shopkeepers, pets).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local npc = entity.nearestNpc()
if npc and npc:isAlive() then
    npc:attack()
end

docs.title: Object
docs.text:
object (global table)

Live query over scene objects (trees, doors, banks, stairs, etc. — "Locs" in OSRS terminology). Distinct from entity (NPCs / players) and grounditem (lootable items on the floor).

Global table

Lives at Lua global scope, not under srs.* — object.nearest(), not srs.object.nearest(). Kept this way for source-compat.

See also

For interaction prefer the higher-level srs.gameobject facade, which returns lighter GameObjectEntry tables and ships a built-in interact() helper.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Returns Every loc, every plane object.all() ActionTarget[] By LocType id object.byId(id) ActionTarget[] By name object.byName(name) ActionTarget[] Closest loc (Chebyshev) object.nearest() ActionTarget \| nil Closest matching name object.nearestByName(name) ActionTarget \| nil LocType cache lookup object.lookup(id) → LocTypeData always returns; check .valid

object.all() is heavy — tens of thousands of rows in a typical city. Prefer byId / byName / nearest*, or filter yourself.

Name lookups are case- and whitespace-insensitive ("Bank booth", "bankbooth", "BANK_BOOTH" all match the same target).

docs.title: LocTypeData
docs.text:
Returned by object.lookup(id). Read-only.

Field Type Notes valid boolean False on cache miss (decoder hasn't touched this id) active boolean True if the LocType declares any menu options name string In-game display name address integer Raw internal address of the LocType; not useful to scripts

A valid=false result usually means the id has never been on screen yet — pan the camera onto an instance and try again.

docs.title: ActionTarget
docs.text: See Entity for the full field/method list. For locs, kind == 3 (TargetKind::Object) and entityId is the LocType id.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Chop the nearest tree
local tree = object.nearestByName("Tree")
if tree then tree:interact("Chop down") end

-- Find every bank booth in the loaded scene
for _, booth in ipairs(object.byName("Bank booth")) do
    log.info(("booth at %d, %d"):format(booth.tileX, booth.tileY))
end

-- Look up a LocType by id
local loc = object.lookup(10355)
if loc.valid then
    log.info(("LocType #10355 = '%s' (active=%s)"):format(
        loc.name, tostring(loc.active)))
end

docs.title: Overlay
docs.text:
srs.overlay

Themed HUD kit layered on Drawing: dark-glass panels, per-skill accent colors, tinted icons, XP rows, animated bars, and level rings. Every call is valid only inside a script.draw(fn) callback — the host drives the frame clock and fonts.

draw-only

Calling any srs.overlay.* function outside a script.draw(fn) callback is undefined — there is no live ImGui frame. The host installs the fonts, advances the frame clock (new_frame) and clears the icon cache itself; scripts never need to.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method names are snake_case.

Method Lua Skill accent color srs.overlay.skill_color(skillInt) → Color Skill default icon srs.overlay.skill_icon(skillInt) → integer Set Custom accent/icon srs.overlay.set_custom(color[, icon=Default]) Frame clock + animation step (host-driven; scripts never call it) srs.overlay.new_frame([dt=-1]) Session runtime string srs.overlay.runtime([seconds=-1]) → string Humanized number srs.overlay.short(v) → string Begin themed panel srs.overlay.begin_panel(id, title, skillInt) → boolean End panel srs.overlay.end_panel() Begin inner card srs.overlay.begin_card([id]) → boolean End card srs.overlay.end_card() Next widget on same row srs.overlay.same_row() Vertical gap srs.overlay.gap([px=-1]) Pulsing status dot + text srs.overlay.status_dot(skillInt, text) Uppercase caption srs.overlay.label(text) Icon + label + value row srs.overlay.stat_row(skillInt, label, value[, icon=Default]) Animated progress bar srs.overlay.bar(skillInt, pct[, h=-1]) Full XP block row srs.overlay.xp_row{skill=, name=, gained=, rate=, level_from=, level_to=, pct=} Labelled chip (mini bar + %) srs.overlay.chip(skillInt, label, pct) Icon + text chip srs.overlay.chip_text(skillInt, iconInt, text) Big level ring srs.overlay.ring(skillInt, pct, bigText, labelText[, d=138[, th=11]]) Compact ring chip srs.overlay.ring_chip(skillInt, name, pct, sub[, icon=Default]) Begin N-column grid srs.overlay.begin_grid(cols) End grid srs.overlay.end_grid()
  • begin_panel / end_panel and begin_card / end_card must always pair — call the end_* regardless of the begin_* return value (same contract as ImGui windows).
  • set_custom sets the accent (and optional icon) used by Skill.Custom; it persists until changed.
  • runtime returns "HH:MM:SS"; pass seconds < 0 to use the internal session accumulator.
  • short humanizes numbers (8420000 → "8.42M", 1438 → "1,438"). short is a fine Lua table key, but some editors/linters prefer the srs.overlay["short"] spelling.
  • bar / chip / ring percentages are in [0, 1]. stat_row auto-dims / and · characters in the value string.
  • gap(px) with px < 0 inserts the standard section gap.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
srs.overlay.Skill — 18 accent identities:

Fishing, Hunter, Cooking, Woodcutting, Mining, Agility, Thieving, Slayer, Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, Magic, Prayer, Crafting, GP, Custom

Not the global Skill enum

srs.overlay.Skill (18 HUD accent identities) is a different enum from the global Skill (24 game skills, see Player). The values do not line up — never pass one where the other is expected.

srs.overlay.Icon — 24 glyphs:

fish, sword, skull, axe, tree, pickaxe, footprints, mask, paw, pot, flame, heart, gem, coins, backpack, clock, timer, target, trending, bolt, arrow, bank, vial, Default

Mixed-case Icon keys

The Lua Icon table keys are lowercase for the glyphs (srs.overlay.Icon.fish) but capitalized for Default (srs.overlay.Icon.Default). Default means "use the accent skill's default icon".

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
xp_row argument table:

Field Type Notes skill integer srs.overlay.Skill.* value; default Custom name string Row caption; omitted/empty = use the skill's name gained integer XP gained; default 0 rate integer XP per hour; default 0 level_from integer Starting level; default 0 level_to integer Next level; default 0 pct number Progress to next level, [0, 1]; default 0

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
script.draw(function()
    local S = srs.overlay.Skill
    if srs.overlay.begin_panel("wc_hud", "Woodcutter", S.Woodcutting) then
        srs.overlay.status_dot(S.Woodcutting, "Chopping")
        srs.overlay.stat_row(S.GP, "Profit", srs.overlay.short(184200))
        srs.overlay.xp_row{
            skill = S.Woodcutting, gained = 12500, rate = 41000,
            level_from = 71, level_to = 72, pct = 0.34,
        }
    end
    srs.overlay.end_panel()  -- always, regardless of begin_panel result
end)

See Drawing for the low-level primitives (srs.draw.*) this kit is built on — anchored overlays, raw draw-list shapes, and input widgets (buttons, sliders, checkboxes).

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
srs.player

Local-player state. Each helper returns a sensible fallback (empty string / -1 / 0) instead of optional so Lua callers don't have to deal with a multi-return shape.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Lua World-tile position srs.player.position() → WorldTile Template-space position srs.player.templatePosition() → WorldTile Display name srs.player.displayName() → string Active animation id srs.player.animation() → int Facing angle srs.player.orientation() → int Carried weight (kg) srs.player.weight() → int Run energy srs.player.runEnergy() → int Set run on/off srs.player.toggleRunEnergy(on) → bool Poison counter (raw) srs.player.poison() → int Is poisoned srs.player.isPoisoned() → bool Is venomed srs.player.isVenomed() → bool Idle ticks counter srs.player.idleTicks() → int Boosted skill level srs.player.skillLevel(Skill) → int Base skill level srs.player.skillBase(Skill) → int Skill XP srs.player.skillXp(Skill) → int XP for a level (static) srs.player.xpForLevel(level) → int Level for total XP (static) srs.player.levelForXp(xp) → int XP remaining to next level srs.player.xpToNextLevel(Skill) → int Progress into current level (0..1) srs.player.levelProgress(Skill) → number Current hitpoints srs.player.hitpoints() → int Max hitpoints srs.player.maxHitpoints() → int Hitpoints percentage srs.player.hpPercent() → int Current prayer points srs.player.prayer() → int Prayer level (base) srs.player.maxPrayer() → int Overhead prayer headicon srs.player.overheadPrayer() → OverheadPrayer Quest completion state srs.player.questState(Quest) → QuestState Quest raw progress srs.player.questProgress(Quest) → int

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
• position — returns a WorldTile of {0, 0, 0} when the player isn't available (pre-login). Callers that care about the difference should check that they are logged in first. Inside an instance this is the raw instance-local tile.
  • templatePosition — same as position outside an instance; inside an instance it maps the raw instance-local tile back through the engine's chunk layout to the template world tile (the wiki coordinate), falling back to position when the conversion can't be made. Pairs with srs.area.isInInstance() to decide raw-vs-template coordinates in instanced content.
  • displayName — the local player's display name; empty string pre-login.
  • animation — current animation id from the active AnimSlot. -1 = idle.
  • orientation — the local player's facing angle, 0–2047, same units and convention as ActionTarget.orientation (see Entity): 0 = S, 512 = W, 1024 = N, 1536 = E. This is the target angle the engine turns toward; the rendered model catches up within a few ticks. -1 pre-login. Compare against a cardinal with a tolerance (math.abs(o - 1024) <= 256 for north).
  • weight — carried weight in kg, as shown by the game.
  • runEnergy — in 0..10000 range (raw network units; divide by 100 for the displayed percentage). -1 if unavailable.
  • poison / isPoisoned / isVenomed — read the game's poison damage counter (VarPlayer 102). poison() returns the raw value: 0 = clean, 1..999999 = poisoned, >= 1000000 = venomed, < 0 = temporary immunity that counts back up toward 0 after an antidote/cure. isPoisoned() is 1..999999; isVenomed() is >= 1000000 (venom is not "poisoned" — check it first). Returns 0 / false when the value can't be read.
  • idleTicks — number of consecutive game ticks the player's active animation has been -1. Reset to 0 the moment any non-idle animation plays.
  • skillLevel / skillBase / skillXp — read the boosted level, base level, or total XP for any skill. Returns 0 when unavailable.
  • hitpoints / maxHitpoints — shorthand for skillLevel(Skill.Hitpoints) / skillBase(Skill.Hitpoints).
  • hpPercent — floor(hitpoints * 100 / maxHitpoints), an integer. Can exceed 100 while boosted (e.g. after an anglerfish or Saradomin brew). Returns 0 when hitpoints aren't readable (e.g. logged out).
  • toggleRunEnergy — despite the name this sets the run state: it reads the current run toggle and returns true without clicking if it already matches on; otherwise it clicks the run orb.
  • prayer / maxPrayer — current prayer points (live, drains with use) + base prayer level. Mirrors srs.prayer.points / srs.prayer.level.
  • overheadPrayer — the local player's active Protect-from headicon. OverheadPrayer.None when no overhead prayer is active or pre-login. See Prayer for the OverheadPrayer enum (a Lua global enum — same values for players and NPCs; NPCs read it via srs.npc.overheadPrayer).
  • questState — completion bucket for a quest (NotStarted / InProgress / Finished). Backed by the game's own quest-status clientscript, so it is correct for every quest with no hand-maintained thresholds. That script must run on the engine thread while your script runs on another thread, so the value is cached and refreshed asynchronously: the first lookup of a given quest returns QuestState.Unknown and kicks off a refresh that lands within a tick or two on its own — no click needed, then stays live. Poll until != Unknown, or just read it each tick. Subsequent reads are instant.
  • questProgress — the raw varbit/varp that increments as a quest advances — i.e. the step number a questing script wants. Thread-safe and instant (a plain var read, no clientscript). 0 before the quest is started; quest-specific value as it advances; -1 for the handful of quests with no single tracked progress var, or when the value isn't readable yet. Use questState for completion; use this for "which step am I on".

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
WorldTile (read-only):

Field Type Notes x integer World X y integer World Y plane integer Plane / level

Methods (Lua, value semantics):

Method Lua Offset copy tile:derive(dx, dy[, dPlane]) → WorldTile Distance ("chebyshev" default, "manhattan", "euclidean") tile:distanceTo(other[, alg]) → number Same plane and Chebyshev distance ≤ r tile:withinRange(other, r) → bool Random tile in the ±rx × ±ry box around this one tile:randomize(rx, ry) → WorldTile Coordinate equality tile:equals(other) → bool (also ==) Debug string tostring(tile) → "WorldTile(x, y, plane)"

Lua constructor

Fields are read-only. Scripts normally obtain a tile from srs.player.position() (or another API that returns tiles), but you can build one with WorldTile.new(x, y[, plane]) (plane defaults to 0). Plain WorldTile(x, y) does not work. Every Lua API that takes a tile also offers (x, y[, plane]) overloads (e.g. srs.camera.rotateToTile(x, y)), so you rarely need to build one.

Skill enum — values match the engine's skill table:

Attack, Defence, Strength, Hitpoints, Ranged, Prayer, Magic, Cooking, Woodcutting, Fletching, Fishing, Firemaking, Crafting, Smithing, Mining, Herblore, Agility, Thieving, Slayer, Farming, Runecraft, Hunter, Construction, Sailing.

In Lua: Skill.Hitpoints, etc. (registered at Lua global scope, same as CameraMode).

Quest enum — every quest the engine tracks (209 generated enumerators), value = stable index. Examples: Quest.CooksAssistant, Quest.DragonSlayerI, Quest.MonkeyMadnessIi, Quest.RecipeForDisaster, Quest.DesertTreasureIiTheFallenEmpire. Registered at Lua global scope (same as Skill).

QuestState enum:

Value Meaning Unknown Not cached yet — questState hasn't primed for this quest. Sentinel; never returned by the engine NotStarted Quest not begun InProgress Quest started, not finished Finished Quest complete

In Lua: QuestState.Finished, etc. (registered at Lua global scope).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local pos = srs.player.position()
log.info(("at %d, %d (plane %d)"):format(pos.x, pos.y, pos.plane))
if srs.player.hitpoints() < srs.player.maxHitpoints() / 2 then
    srs.food.eatBest()
end
if srs.player.idleTicks() > 5 and srs.player.overheadPrayer() == OverheadPrayer.None then
    -- idle and no protection up — do something
end
if srs.player.questState(Quest.CooksAssistant) == QuestState.Finished then
    log.info("Cook's Assistant done")
end

docs.title: PluginSettings
docs.text:
script.setSetting / script.onSettingsButton

Write back to your Lua script's own schema-driven settings — the flat "<groupId>.<rowId>" values that back the schema declared with script.declareSettings.

Different from srs.settings, which reads GAME settings (varbits / varps). This module is about the script's own UI values.

The functions live in the script.* namespace. The write is attributed to the currently firing script (the one whose callback is running); a call that cannot be attributed to a script is silently dropped.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Register a button handler script.onSettingsButton(name, fn) Write one flat setting script.setSetting(key, value)

Register at top level. script.onSettingsButton (and script.onSettingsChanged) attach to the script that is currently loading, so they must run in the top-level chunk. Called later from pulse / onTick / draw they are silently ignored. script.setSetting, by contrast, works from any callback. Registering the same name again replaces the earlier handler.

name is the action string of a settings row whose kind is button. fn takes no arguments.

key is "<groupId>.<rowId>" — the same flat encoding script.onSettingsChanged receives. value may be a boolean, number, string or table, and should match the row's kind: boolean for check, number for number / slider, string for text / select. Written values persist per in-game character.

docs.title: Example — gear-setup capture button
docs.text:
A button row + a text row let a script snapshot the currently worn gear into a textbox:

script.declareSettings {
  groups = {
    { id = "gear", title = "gear setup", open = true, rows = {
      { id = "ids",  label = "Equipped item ids", kind = "text",
        value = "", placeholder = "click Pull to fill", mono = true },
      { id = "pull", label = "Fill from worn gear", kind = "button",
        value = "Pull equipped", action = "pull_gear" },
    }},
  },
}

script.onSettingsButton("pull_gear", function()
  local ids = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(srs.equipment.all()) do ids[#ids + 1] = e.id end
  script.setSetting("gear.ids", table.concat(ids, ","))
end)

docs.title: Threading
docs.text: Button clicks (and therefore script.setSetting calls made from inside a button handler) run on the script worker thread, never the render thread. A slow handler (item-name load, GE / bank calls) cannot freeze the game. Blocking primitives inside the handler release the GIL via the usual helpers so the render thread's script.draw keeps running smoothly.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Script.md — script.declareSettings, script.setSetting / script.onSettingsButton and the schema shape reference (row kinds, per-character storage).
  • Settings.md — GAME settings (varbit / varp) — read-only.

docs.title: Prayer
docs.text:
srs.prayer

Toggle prayers and read state. Backed by the prayer book widget (group 541) for clicks and per-prayer activation varbits for reads.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Remaining prayer points srs.prayer.points() → int Base prayer level srs.prayer.level() → int Display name srs.prayer.name(kind) → string Level requirement srs.prayer.levelRequired(kind) → int Activation varbit id srs.prayer.varbitId(kind) → int Prayer book child id srs.prayer.widgetChild(kind) → int Per-prayer active state srs.prayer.isActive(kind) → bool Is the varbit readable srs.prayer.isReadable(kind) → bool Every active prayer srs.prayer.activeList() → table Raw bitfield mirror srs.prayer.allActiveRaw() → int Unlocked (Rigour etc.) srs.prayer.isUnlocked(kind) → bool Prayer occupying the slot srs.prayer.slotOccupant(kind) → int Usable right now srs.prayer.isAvailable(kind) → bool Best damage prayer srs.prayer.bestOffensive(style) → int Toggle prayer srs.prayer.toggle(kind) → bool Ensure desired state srs.prayer.setActive(kind, on) → bool
  • points is the live prayer-point count (drains with use); level is the base Prayer level.
  • isActive reads the prayer's own activation varbit. It returns false both for "off" and for "couldn't read" — use isReadable to tell those apart.
  • toggle clicks the prayer button to flip its state. It opens the Prayer tab first if needed, returning false that frame (the book doesn't render until the next one). It does not check prayer points, and it is unguarded: two calls in a tick flip the prayer twice.
  • setActive clicks only if currently mismatched, and is the call state-driven code should use — see the rate limit below. It returns true when the prayer is already in the requested state or a click was sent, and false when it declined (cooling down, unreadable varbit, shadowed slot) or the click could not be dispatched.
  • activeList is one varbit read per prayer. That is the cheap "everything at once" read; the client's own bitfield mirror at varbit 4101 (PRAYER_ALLACTIVE) packs the same information, but its bit order isn't published, so it is exposed raw via allActiveRaw rather than decoded on a guess.

setActive is rate-limited per prayer

The activation varbit only flips once the server answers, up to a tick after the click. A caller polling at pulse rate therefore reads "still off" immediately after clicking and would click again, toggling the prayer straight back off — a live log showed two protects alternating every tick before the Gauntlet script added its own per-prayer gate. setActive now suppresses repeat clicks on the same prayer for 1200 ms (two game ticks) and returns false while it is waiting. toggle bypasses the gate.

setActive also refuses — with a throttled log line — to click a prayer whose varbit can't be read at all, instead of clicking forever waiting for a flip that can never be observed.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Prayer constants (srs.prayer.*):

The whole standard prayer book, in level order. widgetChild is the child id inside prayer book group 541; varbit is the activation varbit. NONE (−1) is the "no prayer" value bestOffensive and slotOccupant return.

Lua const Prayer Level Child Varbit THICK_SKIN Thick Skin 1 9 4104 BURST_OF_STRENGTH Burst of Strength 4 10 4105 CLARITY_OF_THOUGHT Clarity of Thought 7 11 4106 SHARP_EYE Sharp Eye 8 27 4122 MYSTIC_WILL Mystic Will 9 30 4123 ROCK_SKIN Rock Skin 10 12 4107 SUPERHUMAN_STRENGTH Superhuman Strength 13 13 4108 IMPROVED_REFLEXES Improved Reflexes 16 14 4109 RAPID_RESTORE Rapid Restore 19 15 4110 RAPID_HEAL Rapid Heal 22 16 4111 PROTECT_ITEM Protect Item 25 17 4112 HAWK_EYE Hawk Eye 26 28 4124 MYSTIC_LORE Mystic Lore 27 31 4125 STEEL_SKIN Steel Skin 28 18 4113 ULTIMATE_STRENGTH Ultimate Strength 31 19 4114 INCREDIBLE_REFLEXES Incredible Reflexes 34 20 4115 PROTECT_MAGIC Protect from Magic 37 21 4116 PROTECT_MISSILE Protect from Missiles 40 22 4117 PROTECT_MELEE Protect from Melee 43 23 4118 EAGLE_EYE Eagle Eye 44 29 4126 MYSTIC_MIGHT Mystic Might 45 32 4127 RETRIBUTION Retribution 46 24 4119 REDEMPTION Redemption 49 25 4120 SMITE Smite 52 26 4121 PRESERVE Preserve 55 37 5466 CHIVALRY Chivalry 60 34 4128 DEADEYE Deadeye 62 29 16090 MYSTIC_VIGOUR Mystic Vigour 63 32 16091 PIETY Piety 70 35 4129 RIGOUR Rigour 74 33 5464 AUGURY Augury 77 36 5465

PrayerStyle constants — which line bestOffensive picks from: STYLE_MELEE, STYLE_RANGED, STYLE_MAGIC. They are prefixed because STYLE_MELEE is 0, the same integer as PROTECT_MAGIC.

The book is not numbered in display order

The prayer book's children are numbered in the interface's own definition order (child = 8 + N), and the ranged/magic prayers plus the later additions were appended after the original set. So Retribution (child 24) sits below Sharp Eye (child 27) in the numbering even though it is far below it in the book. Anything that guesses a child by counting rows will be wrong; the pairing is community-documented, and the three protection prayers are the best-tested of the set.

Eagle Eye / Deadeye and Mystic Might / Mystic Vigour share a button

Deadeye replaces Eagle Eye in the book once unlocked, and Mystic Vigour replaces Mystic Might — one child, two prayers, two varbits. isActive is literal (it reads the prayer you asked about), slotOccupant tells you which of the pair the button currently activates, and isAvailable is false for the one that is currently shadowed. setActive(EAGLE_EYE, true) on an account with Deadeye unlocked refuses and logs, rather than clicking a button whose effect it can't observe.

bestOffensive handles all of this — prefer it over naming a prayer directly when any account might run the script.

Ruinous Powers

The Ruinous Powers book (Varlamore) is a separate interface with its own prayers and its own bitfield mirror (varbit 14827). It is not covered by this module.

docs.title: Overhead prayers (headicons)
docs.text:
Lua global enum OverheadPrayer

The overhead protection-prayer headicon shown above an actor. The enum is registered at global scope — write OverheadPrayer.Missiles, not srs.prayer.OverheadPrayer (no such path exists).

Value Name Meaning -1 None No headicon 0 Melee Protect from Melee 1 Missiles Protect from Missiles 2 Magic Protect from Magic 3 Retribution Retribution 4 Smite Smite 5 Redemption Redemption

The numeric values are the engine's headicon prayer index, and they're identical for players and NPCs.

Readers that return this enum:

  • Local player: srs.player.overheadPrayer() — see Player
  • NPCs: srs.npc.overheadPrayer(target) — see NPC
  • Entity handle: target:overheadPrayer() on ActionTarget — see Entity

Note these read the headicon, not the client's prayer-book state — isActive above is the local prayer-book read, overheadPrayer is what's actually displayed over a head (yours or an NPC's).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if srs.prayer.points() > 0 then
    srs.prayer.setActive(srs.prayer.PROTECT_MISSILE, true)
end

Picking a damage prayer without hard-coding one (Rigour on an account that has it, Eagle Eye on one that doesn't, nothing at all below level 8):

local boost = srs.prayer.bestOffensive(srs.prayer.STYLE_RANGED)
if boost ~= srs.prayer.NONE then
