    srs.prayer.setActive(boost, true)
end

Every entry in the table above has been checked against the live client: each child of group 541 matches the engine's label, and toggling each prayer flips its varbit both ways. The table is re-verified after game updates that move interfaces.

docs.title: Projectiles
docs.text:
srs.projectiles

Read-only enumeration of in-flight projectiles. The common case is "what's about to hit me and when" — use incoming() for that.

incoming() is not filtered to you

The engine keeps one global projectile list, not a per-player one, so incoming() and all() currently return the same snapshot: every projectile in the scene, including ones aimed at other players and at tiles. No per-projectile target field is mapped yet — filter by id when you need to distinguish (at Hunllef, for instance, the magic and ranged attack ids versus everything else).

Cache ids

id is this client's spotanim/graphic cache id. It does not directly equal ids published in community projectile lists — different cache revisions diverge by varying amounts. If you need readable labels, build a per-build mapping table.

Time units

ticksUntilLanding is in game ticks (600 ms each), rounded up from the engine's 50 Hz client-cycle counter (30 cycles per tick) and floored at 0.

Working again on current builds

On some earlier client builds every call on this page returned an empty list, and ticksUntilLanding always read 0. Both are fixed — if you shelved a projectile-driven script because "projectiles don't work", try it again.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Any incoming projectile (cheap) srs.projectiles.isUnderFire() → boolean Incoming list srs.projectiles.incoming() → table Next-to-land srs.projectiles.next() → table \| nil Ticks until next srs.projectiles.ticksUntilNext() → integer All projectiles scene-wide (heavier) srs.projectiles.all() → table
  • isUnderFire is the cheapest check — preferred for tight check-loops.
  • next is the projectile with the lowest absoluteEndCycle, i.e. the next one to land.
  • ticksUntilNext returns -1 when nothing is in flight (a plain number compare instead of a nil check, for ranged-prayer flick logic).
  • all is identical to incoming under the current storage model (one global list). It is kept as a distinct call so it stays correct if a per-target filter is ever added to incoming(). Prefer incoming() for "what's about to hit me" so your script picks up that filter for free; use all() when you explicitly mean scene-wide.

docs.title: Spawn events
docs.text:
Method Lua Subscribe to projectile spawns srs.projectiles.onSpawned(fn) → token Unsubscribe srs.projectiles.offSpawned(token) → boolean

onSpawned fires the instant the engine constructs a projectile — for every projectile in the scene, not just ones aimed at you.

fn receives an event table (see below). The callback runs on the script thread, once per spawned projectile. onSpawned returns a numeric token; pass it to offSpawned to unsubscribe.

Unsubscribing

srs.projectiles.offSpawned(token) removes the callback registered under that token. It is safe to call from inside the callback itself (one-shot listeners). Returns false for an unknown or already-removed token. A full script reload still clears all subscriptions automatically, so a register-once-at-load callback needs no explicit cleanup.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
ProjectileEntry (read-only):

Field Type Notes id integer This client's spotanim cache id animationId integer Anim id from the spotanim def; -1 when it has none framesUntilLanding integer Client cycles until it lands (30 per tick) ticksUntilLanding integer ceil(framesUntilLanding / 30), floored at 0 absoluteEndCycle integer Absolute landing cycle startCycle integer Absolute cycle it starts rendering startCycleDelta integer startCycle - now; > 0 = spawned early, not yet moving packedBytes integer Arc slope used by the engine's ballistic solve

startCycleDelta > 0 means the engine has constructed the projectile but it has not begun travelling — a spawn event can arrive before the thing is visibly in the air. Gate on it if you are timing a dodge off the spawn rather than off ticksUntilLanding.

ProjectileSpawnedEvent (the table passed to the onSpawned callback):

Field Type Notes id integer This client's spotanim cache id cycle integer Animation id from the spotanim def; -1 when it has none pos0, pos1, pos2 integer Raw engine position/height values with no defined meaning — don't build on them wallClock number Wall-clock time of the spawn, in milliseconds

The landing cycle is not on the spawn event; read it from absoluteEndCycle on the next incoming() / next() poll.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Register once at script load; keep the token to unsubscribe later.
local token = srs.projectiles.onSpawned(function(e)
    log.info(("projectile spawned: id=%d"):format(e.id))
end)
-- ... later, when no longer needed:
-- srs.projectiles.offSpawned(token)

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.projectiles.isUnderFire() then
        local t = srs.projectiles.ticksUntilNext()
        log.info(("incoming — lands in %d ticks"):format(t))
    end
end)

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
srs.prompt

The chatbox integer / string input prompt — the "Enter amount:" / "Enter name:" line the engine opens for Withdraw-X, Deposit-X, GE quantity/price, item search, etc. Both the numeric and text variants render in the chatbox message layer (group 162, Chatbox.MES_TEXT child 43; the GE-search style line at MES_TEXT2 child 44), and isOpen is true when either child is rendered; the caller decides amount vs text by which method they call.

The same three calls are also exposed as srs.dialogue.isTextPrompt / enterText / enterAmount — see Dialogue for why a runner must treat this prompt as a blocking state that srs.dialogue.isOpen() does not report. Typing goes through srs.input.typeString (engine input-event queue, human-paced).

Blocks

enterAmount / enterText block: they poll for the prompt to open (server-driven prompts round-trip a tick + RTT), type via the field-input path, then press Enter — with the same timing Bank Withdraw-X / GE use. Call from pulse / onTick, never from draw.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Is the prompt open? srs.prompt.isOpen() → bool Wait for it to open srs.prompt.waitOpen([timeoutMs=2400]) → bool Type a number + Enter srs.prompt.enterAmount(n[, timeoutMs=2400]) → bool Type a string + Enter srs.prompt.enterText(s[, timeoutMs=2400]) → bool

enterAmount / enterText poll for the prompt first (up to timeoutMs) and return false if it never opened. Fire the trigger that opens the prompt (e.g. a Withdraw-X click) before calling them.

enterAmount also returns false for a negative amount, and enterText for an empty string.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
srs.bank.withdrawX answers the Withdraw-X prompt itself, so for a bank withdraw you don't need srs.prompt at all:

srs.bank.withdrawX("Coins", 1337)   -- opens the prompt, types 1337, presses Enter

Use srs.prompt directly when something else opened the prompt — e.g. you fired a Withdraw-X / Deposit-X / "Enter amount" menu or widget click yourself:

-- ... after clicking an option that opens the "Enter amount:" prompt:
if srs.prompt.waitOpen(3000) and srs.prompt.enterAmount(1337) then
    log.info("entered a custom amount")
end

docs.title: RandomEvents
docs.text:
srs.randomEvents

The client runs a random-event handler on its own, for every script — no script needs event logic of its own. Settings are per account and are edited in the launcher only; scripts cannot change them. Scripts can pause the handler for a stretch and read its state.

docs.title: What the handler does
docs.text:
• It watches for a random-event NPC that is targeting your player (another player's event is ignored). Event NPCs are recognised by id for the common events (Genie, Dr Jekyll, Drunken dwarf, Evil Bob, Rick Turpentine, Mysterious Old Man, Pillory guard, Sandwich lady and the rest), and by having a "Dismiss" option.
  • After a short random delay (a few game ticks, so it doesn't react on the spawn tick) it dismisses the NPC.
  • Genie: if the account has a lamp skill set in the launcher, the handler talks to the Genie, takes the lamp, uses it, and picks that skill. With no lamp skill set, the Genie is simply dismissed.
  • By default it only acts while a script or plugin is enabled; a human playing by hand handles their own events. It also only acts while logged in and the break scheduler is running or idle.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Pause handling srs.randomEvents.suspend() Resume handling srs.randomEvents.resume() Is handling paused by a script? srs.randomEvents.isSuspended() → boolean Is the handler acting right now? srs.randomEvents.isHandling() → boolean Current phase srs.randomEvents.phase() → string Account's lamp skill ("" = Genie is dismissed) srs.randomEvents.lampSkill() → string Is handling enabled for this account? srs.randomEvents.isEnabled() → boolean Events handled since the client started srs.randomEvents.handledCount() → integer

suspend() lasts until resume() is called, or until no script or plugin is enabled any more (the override is then cleared). It does not change the account's saved settings.

isHandling() is true while an event is being dismissed, talked to, or its lamp used. While it is true your pulse / onTick callbacks are not called at all, so a script's click can't land on top of the handler's. The short reaction delay before the handler acts (phase Waiting) does not pause your script.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
phase() returns one of:

Value Meaning Idle Nothing to do Waiting Event detected, sitting out the reaction delay Dismissing Dismissing the NPC TalkingGenie Talking to the Genie RubbingLamp Using the lamp ChoosingSkill Picking the skill on the lamp interface

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Don't let the handler interrupt a boss fight
script.onTick(function()
    if inBossFight() then
        if not srs.randomEvents.isSuspended() then srs.randomEvents.suspend() end
    elseif srs.randomEvents.isSuspended() then
        srs.randomEvents.resume()
    end
end)

Always resume

A suspended handler ignores events until you call resume() (or all scripts stop). Don't leave it suspended longer than necessary.

Settings are launcher-only

Enabled, reaction delay, Genie handling and the lamp skill are per-account settings in the launcher. lampSkill() and isEnabled() only report them.

docs.title: RunePouch
docs.text:
srs.runepouch

Read the rune pouch contents and move runes in and out through the pouch window (interface group 190). All slots (regular + divine) are read; slots that don't exist on the player's pouch are simply omitted from contents().

Each slot is two varbits: TYPE (a rune index that the facade maps to the rune's item id) and QUANTITY (1..16k). contents(), quantity() and contains() report rune item ids.

Pouch window

open / close / deposit / withdraw operate on the pouch window and block the calling script for up to a couple of seconds (waiting for the window, or for the typed amount prompt). Reads need no window.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Player carries any pouch srs.runepouch.hasPouch() → bool All non-empty slots srs.runepouch.contents() → RunePouchSlot[] Total quantity of rune srs.runepouch.quantity(runeItemId) → int At least N of rune (min=1) srs.runepouch.contains(runeItemId [, min]) → bool Pouch window showing? srs.runepouch.isOpen() → bool Open the pouch window srs.runepouch.open() → bool Close the pouch window srs.runepouch.close() → bool Backpack → pouch srs.runepouch.deposit(runeItemId [, amount]) → bool Pouch → backpack srs.runepouch.withdraw(runeItemId [, amount]) → bool

hasPouch checks the 4 pouch item ids (regular / divine, plain / noted) against the inventory, and the 2 un-noted ids against worn equipment (cheap).

contents returns up to 6 entries (4 standard + 2 divine) — empty slots are omitted, so #contents() equals the number of active runes.

The pouch varbits are registered for you when the API loads, so even the very first contents() / quantity() read already has values.

docs.title: Pouch window
docs.text:
• open() uses the pouch's inventory "Open" op and waits up to about 2 s for the window; returns true when the window is showing. The pouch must be in the backpack.
  • close() clicks the window's Close button (Escape as a fallback) and waits about 1.2 s.
  • deposit / withdraw require the window to be open. amount is 1, 5, any other n (uses the Store-X / Withdraw-X typed prompt, which blocks for about 2 s), or <= 0 for All. amount may be omitted (= All). They return true once the click (and typed amount) has been sent — poll quantity() to confirm the result. They return false (and print the window's cells to the console) when the rune isn't on the source side of the window.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Item ids (srs.runepouch.*):

Lua const Value Item RUNE_POUCH_ID 12791 Rune pouch RUNE_POUCH_NOTED_ID 12792 Rune pouch (noted) DIVINE_POUCH_ID 27281 Divine rune pouch DIVINE_POUCH_NOTED_ID 27282 Divine rune pouch (noted)

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
RunePouchSlot (read-only):

Field Type Notes index integer 0..5 (slot index within the pouch) runeItemId integer 0 if empty quantity integer Stack qty

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if srs.runepouch.hasPouch() then
    for _, slot in ipairs(srs.runepouch.contents()) do
        log.info(("pouch slot %d: rune %d x%d")
            :format(slot.index, slot.runeItemId, slot.quantity))
    end
end

-- Fewer than 100 natures left? Go restock.
if srs.runepouch.hasPouch() and not srs.runepouch.contains(561, 100) then
    log.info("low on nature runes")
end

-- Top up natures from the backpack (blocks briefly while the window opens)
if srs.runepouch.open() then
    srs.runepouch.deposit(561)          -- amount omitted = All
    srs.runepouch.withdraw(563, 5)      -- Withdraw-5 law runes
    srs.runepouch.close()
end

docs.title: Sailing
docs.text:
srs.sailing

Boat state, helm and sail controls, the cargo hold, and the port-task notice board for the Sailing skill.

A boat is its own small world with its own scene, separate from the main map. The boat you are standing on is reported by boat(); every boat in view (yours, other players', and static moored ships) is reported by boats(). Boat positions are in main-world tiles.

Steering works by sending an absolute heading from 0 to 15 (16 compass points: 0 = south, 4 = west, 8 = north, 12 = east). You do not click the on-screen markers yourself; setHeading / steerTowards send the bearing for you. The boat then turns toward it one step at a time, so the reported heading lags the command by a few seconds.

Interface-driven calls (sails, speed, board, cargo hold) operate on panels that must already be rendered. The API never opens side tabs for you; open the right tab from your script first, otherwise these calls return false.

docs.title: Boat state
docs.text:
Method Lua Boat the local player is aboard (nil if none) srs.sailing.boat() → table \| nil Every boat in the scene, including yours srs.sailing.boats() → table Solid hull tiles of a boat, as {forward, right} offsets (your boat if id omitted) srs.sailing.hull([id]) → table Is the local player on a boat srs.sailing.isOnBoat() → bool Raw "operating a facility" value (varbit 19105) srs.sailing.lockedFacility() → integer Is the player at the helm (lockedFacility == 3) srs.sailing.isAtHelm() → bool

lockedFacility is non-zero while you operate any boat facility; 3 is the value seen at the helm.

hull([id]) returns a list of { forward = number, right = number } tables: the solid hull tiles of the boat's own scene as tile offsets from the boat's position (forward is positive toward the bow, right positive toward starboard). With no argument it describes your boat; pass a boat id from boats() for any other. It returns an empty table when you are not aboard (no argument) or the id is unknown.

docs.title: Helm and steering
docs.text:
Method Lua Take the wheel (op 1 on your boat's helm) srs.sailing.interactHelm() → bool Heading (0..15) from one tile to another; -1 if identical srs.sailing.headingTo(fromX, fromY, toX, toY) → integer Command an absolute heading (0..15). Needs the helm srs.sailing.setHeading(heading) → bool Steer toward a world tile srs.sailing.steerTowards(tileX, tileY) → bool
  • setHeading returns false for a heading outside 0..15, when you are not aboard a boat, or when the boat cannot be projected onto the screen. It must be called while you are at the helm (see isAtHelm).
  • steerTowards computes headingTo(boat, target) and sends it. It returns true without sending anything when the boat is already at the target tile or already pointing the right way, so it is safe to call every pulse. It returns false when you are not aboard.
  • interactHelm returns false if no helm is found on your boat.

docs.title: Sails and speed
docs.text:
Method Lua Set / unset sails (one toggle) srs.sailing.toggleSails() → bool Lower speed one step srs.sailing.lowerSpeed() → bool Raise speed one step srs.sailing.raiseSpeed() → bool

Setting sails from a stop goes straight to top speed. All three need the Sailing side tab open on its Facilities sub-tab (interface 937, component 25); they return false when that panel is not rendered. true means the click was dispatched, not that the boat changed state; read boat().speed to confirm.

docs.title: Cargo hold
docs.text:
Method Lua Op 1 on your boat's cargo hold srs.sailing.interactCargoHold() → bool Is the cargo-hold interface (943) open srs.sailing.isCargoHoldOpen() → bool Stacks in the open hold srs.sailing.cargoHoldItems() → table Withdraw the stack of an item id srs.sailing.withdrawCargo(itemId) → bool

Using the hold while carrying cargo deposits it directly; with nothing to deposit it opens the cargo-hold interface. cargoHoldItems is empty while the interface is closed. withdrawCargo returns false if the item is not in the open hold or its cell is not rendered.

docs.title: Port tasks
docs.text:
Method Lua Occupied task slots srs.sailing.portTasks() → table Task slots your Sailing level allows (1..5) srs.sailing.taskCapacity() → integer

taskCapacity is derived from base Sailing level: 1 / 7 / 28 / 56 / 84 give 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 slots. It is the level cap only; any additional unlocked slots are not counted.

docs.title: Notice board and task offers
docs.text:
Method Lua Is the notice board (941) open srs.sailing.isBoardOpen() → bool Cards on the open board srs.sailing.boardOffers() → table Open a card's task popup by dbrow srs.sailing.openOffer(dbrow) → bool Is the task-info popup (942) open srs.sailing.isOfferOpen() → bool Parsed contents of the open popup srs.sailing.offerDetails() → table \| nil Accept the open offer srs.sailing.acceptOffer() → bool Back from the popup to the board srs.sailing.backFromOffer() → bool Close the board / popup srs.sailing.closeBoard() → bool
  • boardOffers is empty while the board is closed. Offers are identified by dbrow; pass that to openOffer.
  • acceptOffer returns false without clicking when every task slot you are allowed is already in use (the server would refuse it silently), and when the popup is not open.
  • backFromOffer returns false when the popup is not open.
  • closeBoard presses Escape and returns true immediately if neither the board nor the popup is open.

docs.title: BoatInfo
docs.text:
Returned by boat() / boats(): each boat is a plain table with these fields.

Field Type Notes id integer Boat id (also the key of its own scene) x, y integer World tile plane integer Plane (currently always 0) fineX, fineY integer World position in 1/128-tile units (sub-tile precision) heading integer Direction the boat is facing now, 0..15; -1 = unreadable orientation integer Facing in 0..2047 units (128 per heading step); -1 = unreadable speed integer Fine units per tick (128 = 1 tile/tick); 0 at rest sizeX, sizeY integer The boat's own scene size in tiles. An upper bound on the hull; the long side lies along the heading. Useful for steering clear of other boats ownerType integer 0 = not a player's boat (static or moored ship, solid), 1 = another player's boat (you sail through it), 2 = yours, -1 = unreadable configId integer Boat type id isLocal boolean The local player is aboard this boat renderOrientation integer Smooth on-screen facing in 0..2047 units; -1 = unreadable targetX, targetY integer Present only when the server position is known. World tile where the server has the boat this tick (leads x/y by up to one tick) targetFineX, targetFineY integer Same condition. Server position in 1/128-tile units targetOrientation integer Same condition. Heading the current tick's step is on, 0..2047 stepX, stepY integer Same condition. This tick's step in fine units (128 = 1 tile): the boat's real velocity stepFresh boolean Same condition. stepX/stepY are only current while this is true; at rest the last step stays behind

docs.title: BoardOffer
docs.text:
One card on the open notice board, as a table.

Field Type Notes card integer 0-based card position (row-major) dbrow integer Task row id; pass to openOffer. -1 if unreadable name string Card title with colour tags removed, e.g. "Pandemonium steel delivery" level integer Sailing level printed on the card levelMet boolean Your base Sailing level is at least level badgeSprite integer Requirement-badge sprite id (7107 / 7108); diagnostic only isCourier boolean Name ends in "delivery" (bounties end in "bounty")

Note

dbrow is the task's board row. It is not the same number as PortTaskSlot.taskId, which is the id stored in your task slot varbits.

docs.title: OfferDetails
docs.text:
Parsed from the open task-info popup; returned as a table.

Field Type Notes name string Task title level integer Sailing level required cargo string Cargo item name location string Where the cargo is collected destination string Where it is delivered quantity integer Amount of cargo description string Remaining flavour text (lines joined with \n)

docs.title: CargoItem
docs.text: Field Type Notes slot integer Cell index in the hold grid itemId integer Item id qty integer Stack quantity

docs.title: PortTaskSlot
docs.text:
Returned by portTasks(); only occupied slots (task id non-zero) appear.

Field Type Notes slot integer 0..4 taskId integer Task id held in that slot (see the note under BoardOffer) cargoTaken integer Cargo collected so far cargoDelivered integer Cargo delivered so far

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local TARGET_X, TARGET_Y = 3050, 3210

script.pulse(function()
    local boat = srs.sailing.boat()
    if not boat then return end

    if not srs.sailing.isAtHelm() then
        srs.sailing.interactHelm()
        return
    end

    -- Point at the destination (no-op if already pointing there).
    srs.sailing.steerTowards(TARGET_X, TARGET_Y)

    -- List static (solid) ships in view.
    for _, other in ipairs(srs.sailing.boats()) do
        if not other.isLocal and other.ownerType == 0 then
            log.info(("static ship at %d,%d size %dx%d"):format(
                other.x, other.y, other.sizeX, other.sizeY))
        end
    end
end)

-- Taking a task from an open notice board:
script.onTick(function()
    if srs.sailing.isBoardOpen() and #srs.sailing.portTasks() < srs.sailing.taskCapacity() then
        for _, offer in ipairs(srs.sailing.boardOffers()) do
            if offer.levelMet and offer.isCourier then
                srs.sailing.openOffer(offer.dbrow)
                break
            end
        end
    end
    if srs.sailing.isOfferOpen() then
        local d = srs.sailing.offerDetails()
        if d then log.info(d.name .. ": " .. d.cargo .. " x" .. d.quantity) end
        srs.sailing.acceptOffer()
    end
end)

Open the right tab first

toggleSails, lowerSpeed and raiseSpeed need the Sailing side tab open on Facilities. The board, popup and cargo-hold calls need their interface open. None of these calls open a tab or interface for you; they return false when the panel is not rendered.

A returned true means dispatched

Every action call returns true when the click or packet was sent. It does not confirm the game accepted it. Poll boat(), portTasks(), cargoHoldItems() or the is*Open calls to confirm, and throttle repeated calls rather than firing one every pulse.

Heading lags the command

setHeading sets the boat's target bearing. The boat turns one step at a time, so boat().heading takes a few seconds to catch up. Do not treat a mismatch as a failed command.

docs.title: Screenshot
docs.text:
srs.screenshot

Save a screenshot of the game canvas as a PNG. The capture is the game window's client area as the game rendered it, not the launcher window around it. Files go to the screenshots folder in the SafeRS install directory, which is created on the first save.

By default the SafeRS overlay (script HUDs, ESP, the debug panel) is left out of the image. Pass overlay = true to keep it.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Save a screenshot named by timestamp srs.screenshot() → string\|nil Save with a name srs.screenshot(name) → string\|nil Save with a name, choosing the overlay srs.screenshot(name, opts) → string\|nil Save with options, no name srs.screenshot(opts) → string\|nil

srs.screenshot is a plain function (not a table). The first argument is either the name or the options table.

The file is named <name> <yyyy-mm-dd_HH-MM-SS-mmm>.png, or just the timestamp when no name is given. Characters a file name can't hold become _, and the name is cut to 80 bytes.

Returns the full path (UTF-8) the PNG is being written to. When the call is refused — 8 captures are already pending, or capture isn't initialised yet — it returns nil.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Options (a table, all keys optional):

Field Type Default Notes overlay boolean false Include the SafeRS overlay in the image

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Asynchronous: the frame is captured on the next render and encoded off the game thread, so the file appears a moment after the call returns. The call itself never blocks, so it's safe from draw as well as pulse/onTick.
  • With the game window minimised there is no canvas; the capture fails and no file is written.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
srs.events.on("levelUp", function(e)
    srs.screenshot(("Level %d (skill %d)"):format(e.level, e.skill))
end)

-- With the script's overlay in the picture
local path = srs.screenshot("Session end", { overlay = true })
if path then print("Saved " .. path) end

Discord screenshots

The launcher's Notifications settings have a Screenshot column: for the event kinds ticked there, the Discord post carries a screenshot taken when the event fired. Those are sent to the webhook only and are never written to the screenshots folder. Scripts don't need to call anything for this.

docs.title: Script lifecycle
docs.text:
script.* / log.* / srs.wait (global tables)

Everything a Lua script uses to hook into the engine: lifecycle callbacks, script metadata + settings, logging, tick suspension, and the sandboxed module loader.

docs.title: Lifecycle callbacks
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Per-frame callback (~60 Hz) script.pulse(fn) Runs every render frame Per-game-tick callback (~600 ms) script.onTick(fn) Runs once per server tick One-shot next-tick callback script.nextTick(fn) Fires once on the next tick rollover Overlay draw callback script.draw(fn) Per-frame, inside a live ImGui frame — srs.draw / srs.overlay are only valid here

pulse and onTick are both optional — register whichever cadence fits. Use onTick for game logic (actions, state machines) and pulse only when you genuinely need frame-rate polling.

There is no script.onLoad. The top-level chunk is the load hook: statements outside any callback run once when the script is installed. See Install vs start for what that means in practice.

docs.title: Install vs start
docs.text:
A script has three states, not two. The sidebar's Load button installs a script; the Enabled checkbox in its settings panel is the user's start / stop control. A running script can also stop itself with script.stop.

State Set by Meaning prepared sidebar Load Source is in the client and the top chunk has run at least once, so declareInfo / declareSettings have landed and the settings form renders. Sticky across enable/disable and across a Lua VM rebuild. loaded install, or the VM rebuild The chunk is live in the current lua_State. Cleared on disable, restored by the rebuild. enabled the Enabled checkbox The only state that lets callbacks fire (cleared by unticking the box or by script.stop()). A script that is loaded but not enabled runs nothing.

The sidebar row shows Configure once a script is loaded || prepared, and its badge reads loaded vs running. Streamed SDN scripts install on load like every other script — they no longer auto-start.

Your top chunk runs at install time, not at start

The gap between Load and Enabled can be minutes. Anything the top chunk does — capturing a timestamp, baselining srs.stats, snapshotting inventory, reading the player's position — happens at install, against whatever the game state was back then, and is not redone when the user finally starts the script.

Keep the top chunk to declarations (declareInfo, declareSettings, require, callback registration, constant tables). Put "start of run" work in a first-tick guard:

local started = false
script.onTick(function()
    if not started then
        started = true
        srs.stats.reset()       -- real start of the run
    end
    -- ... per-tick logic
end)

Callback registration appends — never register conditionally

script.pulse / onTick / draw append to the callback list. The host does not re-run an already-live chunk when you enable a prepared script, precisely so registrations aren't duplicated. Registering from inside a callback (rather than at the top level) defeats that and your handler fires twice per tick. Register once, at the top level.

docs.title: Script control
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Stop this script script.stop(reason?) Turns the script off, exactly as if the user unticked Enabled

script.stop returns immediately: the callback that called it runs to its end, then no pulse / onTick / nextTick / draw of this script fires again and the engine disables it. reason (optional string) is logged and shown in the launcher as the script row's stop reason. It applies to the calling script (or the script being loaded, when called from the top chunk). The user can start the script again from its settings panel.

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.isFull() then
        return script.stop("inventory full")
    end
    -- ...
end)

docs.title: Metadata and settings
docs.text: Method Lua Notes Declare settings schema script.declareSettings(schemaTable) Top-level only — silently no-ops outside script load Declare script info script.declareInfo({name=, author=, version=, description=}) Top-level only Read current settings script.settings() → table Empty table if the calling script can't be attributed Settings-changed callback script.onSettingsChanged(fn(settingsTable)) Top-level only — silently no-ops from inside a callback. Fires when the user edits settings in the client UI, and once after the schema defaults are merged in Settings button handler script.onSettingsButton(name, fn) Top-level only — runs fn when the user clicks a button row whose action equals name Set one setting value script.setSetting("group.row", value) Writes a flat value back to the UI + saved config; use inside a button handler

docs.title: Settings schema shape
docs.text:
declareSettings takes { groups = { … } }; each group is { id, title, open, rows = { … } } and each row is { id, label, kind, … }. Settings are stored flat as "<groupId>.<rowId>" and saved per in-game character — different characters keep independent configs.

Supported row kinds:

kind Extra fields Renders as check — Toggle select options (strings or {id,label}) Dropdown number min, max, step, suffix Numeric field (with unit suffix) slider min, max, step, suffix Slider with its value shown next to the track text placeholder, maxLength, mono Text field (own line; mono = monospace, for id lists) button action, value (button caption) Button — holds no value; clicking fires onSettingsButton(action)

docs.title: Gear-setup example
docs.text:
A button row + a text row let a script pull the currently worn gear into a textbox:

script.declareSettings({
  groups = {
    { id = "gear", title = "gear setup", open = true, rows = {
      { id = "ids",  label = "Equipped item ids", kind = "text",
        placeholder = "click Pull to fill", mono = true },
      { id = "pull", label = "Fill from worn gear", kind = "button",
        value = "Pull equipped", action = "pull_gear" },
    }},
  },
})

script.onSettingsButton("pull_gear", function()
  local ids = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(srs.equipment.all()) do ids[#ids + 1] = e.id end
  script.setSetting("gear.ids", table.concat(ids, ","))
end)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Info line log.info(msg) Appends [INFO] msg to the engine output buffer Warning line log.warn(msg) [WARN] prefix Error line log.error(msg) [ERROR] prefix Print print(...) Overridden: tab-concatenated tostring() of each arg, to the engine output buffer — not stdout Append to a file log.file(name, line) → string Appends line + CRLF to %TEMP%\safers_<name>.log; returns the full path

The only logging APIs

log.info/warn/error, log.file, and the overridden print are the whole surface. There is no srs.log.* and no osrs.print — code using those names errors at call time.

docs.title: log.file — durable output
docs.text:
The engine output buffer is a ring the user scrolls. That is right for progress messages and useless for a run that emits hundreds of lines and has to survive the client closing — a validation sweep, a long harvest, an overnight session's error trail.

log.file is the one file-writing primitive scripts get (io is deliberately absent from the sandbox). It is deliberately narrow:

  • name is sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9_-], truncated to 64 chars, and always lands in %TEMP% — a script cannot choose an arbitrary path or escape the directory.
  • Every call opens, appends, flushes, and closes. A run that crashes still leaves its evidence on disk.
  • Returns the resolved path (empty string if the file could not be opened) so a script can tell the user where its output went.
local path
for _, e in ipairs(entity.npcs()) do
    path = log.file("npc_survey", ("%s\t%d,%d"):format(e.name, e.tileX, e.tileY))
end
log.info("survey written to " .. tostring(path))

Open-append-close per line is not free — it is fine for a few thousand lines over a session, not for per-frame logging from pulse.

docs.title: Waits (tick suspension)
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Wait N ticks srs.wait([ticks=1]) Mutes this script for N ticks Wait for condition srs.waitUntil(predicateFn[, timeoutTicks=0]) timeoutTicks=0 = no timeout

wait is a suspension gate, not a coroutine sleep

srs.wait(n) mutes this script's pulse / onTick / nextTick callbacks for n ticks — draw keeps firing. It does not interrupt the currently running callback: code after the call still executes. The idiom is srs.wait(n); return. Both wait and waitUntil are silent no-ops outside a firing callback.

  • srs.waitUntil(fn) releases when the predicate returns truthy; if the predicate throws, the wait releases (fail-open) rather than hanging the script.
  • There is no global sleep or scriptSleep.

docs.title: Module loading (require)
docs.text:
require(mod) is replaced with a sandboxed bundle loader:

  • require("a.b") resolves a/b.lua, then a/b/init.lua, from the current bundle's in-memory files only — no filesystem access, no loadlib.
  • Results are cached per bundle; requiring the same module twice returns the cached value.
  • Calling require outside a bundle context (e.g. from a single-file script) or for a missing module throws an error.

docs.title: Available Lua stdlib
docs.text: Open libraries: base, string, math, table, os. Not available: io, package (require is replaced — see above), coroutine, utf8, debug.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
script.declareInfo{ name = "Miner", author = "me", version = "1.0",
                    description = "Powermines iron" }

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.isFull() then
        srs.inventory.dropAll("Iron ore")
        srs.wait(2)  -- mute onTick for 2 ticks; code below still runs
        return
    end
    log.info("Ticking, slots free: " .. srs.inventory.emptySlots())
end)

script.draw(function()
    -- srs.draw / srs.overlay calls are valid only here
end)

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
srs.session

Declare the stats your script wants tracked on the SafeRS website. Every value you declare shows up on the user's Script Stats page for this run: live while it runs, then in their history and lifetime totals per script.

XP is measured by the client on its own while your script runs, so don't report it. The reserved key profit (always gp) also counts toward the platform's "gold earned" figure and your plugin page's totals; every other key is shown only to the user who ran the script.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Set a number stat srs.session.stat(key, value) Set a number stat with a label / kind srs.session.stat(key, value, opts) Set a text stat srs.session.stat(key, "text") Set a text stat with a label srs.session.stat(key, "text", { label = ... }) Forget every stat declared for this run srs.session.reset()

The type of value picks the stat: a number is a number stat, a string is a text stat.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Values are the session total so far, not deltas. profit may be negative.
  • Calls only overwrite the latest value in client memory; nothing is sent per call. The client ships changed values with its regular heartbeat (about every 3 minutes), so it is fine to call these every pulse or onTick.
  • A run is one start → stop of your script. Stopping and starting it again begins a new run with no stats; a break pause does not end the run.
  • Stats belong to the script whose callback is running (the top-level chunk counts too); calls from anywhere else are ignored.
  • Scripts loaded from disk are tracked under their file name and show on the user's own page only; public totals count published plugins.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
SessionStatOptions (a table, all keys optional):

Field Type Default Notes label string the key Display name on the website (up to 48 characters shown) kind string "count" How the value is shown and totalled, see below

Kinds:

Kind Shown as Lifetime total count 1,234 Sum gp 1.2M gp Sum xp 1.2M xp Sum duration value in seconds, shown 1h 23m Sum rate 412 /hr Last value percent 87% Last value

Text stats are kept as is (up to 64 characters shown) and the lifetime view keeps the last value.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• key: lowercase letters, digits, _ and ., 1–32 characters. Other keys are ignored.
  • At most 24 keys per run; extra keys are ignored.
  • profit is always treated as gp, whatever kind you pass. For loot-based scripts, gross loot value counts as profit.
  • Rates are capped server-side, so implausible values are not credited.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local made, profit = 0, 0

local function report()
    srs.session.stat("bars", made, { label = "Bars made" })
    srs.session.stat("profit", profit, { kind = "gp" })
    srs.session.stat("task", "Gold bars", { label = "Current task" })
end

script.onTick(function()
    -- ... smelt, update made/profit ...
    report()
end)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
srs.settings

Read game settings via varbits / varps / varc. This module is read-only: raw readers plus a few named convenience helpers. (It is unrelated to your script's own configurable settings, see Script.)

docs.title: Raw reads
docs.text:
Each reader has a "soft" variant (0 / -1 on miss) and a "present?-aware" variant (returns nil on miss).

Method Lua Raw varbit (0 on miss) srs.settings.varbit(id) → integer Varbit, present?-aware srs.settings.tryVarbit(id) → integer \| nil Raw varp (0 on miss) srs.settings.varp(id) → integer Varp, present?-aware srs.settings.tryVarp(id) → integer \| nil Raw varc int (-1 on miss) srs.settings.varcInt(id) → integer Varc, present?-aware srs.settings.tryVarcInt(id) → integer \| nil

The varc getter already returns -1 as its "missing or wrong type" sentinel, so the raw variant gives -1 for both "not wired" and "unset".

First varbit read is empty

Varbit values are served from a snapshot that only starts tracking an id the first time you ask for it. The very first varbit(id) / tryVarbit(id) for an id therefore returns 0 / nil; later calls return the real value. Read the ids you need once early (for example in your first onTick) before relying on them.

docs.title: Named convenience
docs.text:
Conservative defaults (false / 0) when unresolved.

Method Lua Shift-drop enabled srs.settings.isShiftDropEnabled() → boolean Roofs hidden srs.settings.areRoofsHidden() → boolean Run-toggle on srs.settings.isRunEnabled() → boolean Current spellbook srs.settings.spellbook() → integer

spellbook() returns the varbit 4070 value:

Value Spellbook 0 Standard 1 Ancient 2 Lunar 3 Arceuus

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if not srs.settings.isRunEnabled() and srs.player.runEnergy() > 4000 then
    srs.player.toggleRunEnergy(true)
end
-- raw varbit read with a present?-aware variant
local v = srs.settings.tryVarbit(4070)
if v ~= nil then
    log.info("spellbook varbit = " .. v)
end

docs.title: Shop
docs.text:
srs.shop

Read shop stock, buy from the stock grid and sell from the side inventory. Stock is read from the shop's stock grid (Shopmain.ITEMS, widget 300/16) — each shop has its own inventory id, so there is no single container to read; the grid always mirrors whichever shop is open. The sell side is the player-inventory mirror in group 301.

Per-item clicks use the same recipe as Bank per-item withdraw: a CC_OP on the grid cell (dyn child of Shopmain.ITEMS (300, 16) or the Shopside inventory (301, 0)), routed through the engine's action dispatcher with the input spoof. No packets are built by the script API.

Buy / sell not yet verified in game

buy / sell are built on the same approach as the Bank per-item withdraw, but have not been tested against a live shop. Menu positions are read from each slot's own action list; the fallback table (Value = 1, 1 = 2, 5 = 3, 10 = 4, 50 = 5) and the Buy X / preset flows are unconfirmed. Test on a cheap item before relying on them in a script.

docs.title: State
docs.text: Method Lua Is shop open srs.shop.isOpen() → boolean

docs.title: Stock reads
docs.text:
Method Lua All stock srs.shop.stock() → table Has stock by id srs.shop.hasStock(id) → boolean Has stock by name srs.shop.hasStock(name) → boolean Stock count by id srs.shop.stockCount(id) → integer Stock count by name srs.shop.stockCount(name) → integer At-least-N in stock srs.shop.hasMinimumStock(id, min) → boolean

Name lookups match the item's in-game display name (case- and whitespace-insensitive substring).

stock() returns an empty list while the shop is closed. The slot field on returned items is the index into the shop's stock grid (top-left = 0, row-major). Out-of-stock entries (quantity 0) stay in the list; buy skips them.

docs.title: Per-item buy / sell
docs.text:
Method Lua Buy N of an item srs.shop.buy(id\|name[, qty = 1]) → boolean Sell N of an item srs.shop.sell(id\|name[, qty = 1]) → boolean

buy clicks the stock slot holding the item; sell clicks the backpack slot holding it (the shop-side inventory). Both need the shop open and return false when the item isn't in stock / in the backpack, the slot isn't rendered, or the click doesn't fire.

Quantity semantics — the slot's own right-click ops decide how qty is delivered:

  • Buy 1 / 5 / 10 / 50 (the standard shop menu): an exact op fires when qty matches one. Otherwise the largest ops ≤ qty fire in turn (7 = Buy 5, Buy 1, Buy 1), one per game tick — the call blocks for (clicks − 1) ticks. It never over-buys on the standard menu (a slot with no Buy 1 op would fire its smallest op instead); if stock (or the stack being sold) runs out mid-way it stops early and still returns true for the clicks that fired.
  • Buy X / Sell X (when the UI exposes it): one click, then the amount typed into the chatbox prompt (like srs.bank.withdrawX).
  • bare Buy / Sell (quantity-preset UI): the sticky preset is set via setQuantity to cover qty (X + typed amount when no preset matches), then the slot is clicked once.

When the slot's action list can't be read (widget data not ready) the standard identifier table is used: Value = 1, 1 = 2, 5 = 3, 10 = 4, 50 = 5.

true means the click(s) were dispatched, not that the trade happened — coins, stock and a full backpack are server-side outcomes. Poll stockCount / srs.inventory.count to confirm, and throttle the call (one per few ticks) rather than firing it every pulse.

Name lookups match the item's in-game display name the same way the stock reads do (case- and whitespace-insensitive substring); pass an id when two stocked items share a substring (e.g. Pot vs Pot lid).

docs.title: Quantity preset
docs.text:
Sticky across subsequent buy/sell clicks. Maps to the 1 / 5 / 10 / 50 / X buttons at the bottom of the shop UI. buy / sell only rely on it when the slot exposes a bare Buy / Sell op (see above).

Method Lua Set quantity srs.shop.setQuantity(q) → boolean

Quantity constants (srs.shop.*): ONE, FIVE, TEN, FIFTY, X.

Quantity enum differs from Bank / DepositBox

Shop quantity has FIFTY and no ALL; Bank / DepositBox have ALL and no FIFTY. The constants are per-module — don't pass one module's value to another.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Widget topology (for use with Widget):

Widget Group Child Notes Shop interface 300 — Shop widget group Stock grid (Shopmain.ITEMS) 300 16 Dyn children = stock slots Sell side (Shopside) 301 0 Player-inventory mirror; dyn children = backpack slots

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if srs.shop.isOpen() then
    for _, item in ipairs(srs.shop.stock()) do
        log.info(("slot %d: id=%d x%d"):format(item.slot, item.id, item.quantity))
    end
    if srs.shop.hasStock("Karamjan rum") and srs.inventory.count("Karamjan rum") == 0 then
        srs.shop.buy("Karamjan rum")          -- Buy 1
    end
    if srs.inventory.count("Pot") >= 7 then
        srs.shop.sell("Pot", 7)               -- Sell 5, Sell 1, Sell 1 (blocks ~2 ticks)
    end
end

docs.title: Spells
docs.text:
srs.spells

Static metadata for OSRS spells. Pure data; casting logic lives in Magic.

The table covers 50 Standard-book spells (the 20 strike → surge combat spells, alchemy and other utility spells, 8 teleports, and the NPC / ground-item target spells), the 16 Ancient Magicks combat spells, and the full Lunar (44) and Arceuus (44) books. Standard-book spells other than those listed are not populated, and the Ancient book's non-combat spells (teleports, etc.) are not in the table.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Spell metadata srs.spells.info(s) → SpellInfo Lookup by name srs.spells.byName(name) → SpellInfo \| nil Enum lookup by name srs.spells.idByName(name) → int \| nil All spells in a book srs.spells.inBook(book) → table

byName / idByName are case-insensitive: an exact name match wins, otherwise the first substring match in table order is returned (so "Strike" resolves to Wind Strike). info returns an empty record (name == "") for a value outside the table. inBook returns every populated entry for that book (Standard 50, Ancient 16, Lunar 44, Arceuus 44). byName returns the metadata record; idByName resolves the Spell enum value itself, ready to feed into srs.magic.cast / srs.magic.canCast.

Use idByName for casting, byName for metadata

srs.spells.byName returns a SpellInfo (metadata), not a Spell enum — so idByName is the name → enum path for casting: it returns the Spell enum value srs.magic.cast / srs.magic.canCast take, or nil if nothing matches.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
srs.stats

A lightweight session XP / runtime tracker for a script's stat panel. It captures a baseline — per-skill XP + level and a start timestamp — the first time it's accessed while logged in, then reports gained-since-baseline and extrapolated per-hour rates, computed live on demand (no per-tick bookkeeping).

Baseline

The baseline is process-wide and primed lazily on first access. Call srs.stats.reset() at your script's start for a clean measurement. XP that goes down (an account swap) clamps to 0.

Reset on first tick, not in the top chunk

A Lua script's top-level chunk runs at install time (sidebar Load), which can be many minutes before the user actually starts it — see Install vs start. A bare srs.stats.reset() at the top of the file therefore baselines the XP counter at Load, and the session readout counts all the idle time in between. Do it once from the first onTick instead:

local baselined = false
script.onTick(function()
    if not baselined then srs.stats.reset(); baselined = true end
    -- ...
end)

Loot tracking

Item / loot tracking is intentionally left to scripts on top of the srs.events "inventoryChanged" feed — cumulative-gain vs net is a policy the script should own. Accumulate e.quantityDelta > 0 per e.itemId.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Re-baseline now srs.stats.reset() Seconds since baseline srs.stats.runtime() → integer XP gained in a skill srs.stats.xpGained(skill) → integer Total XP gained srs.stats.totalXpGained() → integer XP/hour for a skill srs.stats.xpPerHour(skill) → number Total XP/hour srs.stats.totalXpPerHour() → number Real levels gained srs.stats.levelsGained(skill) → integer

skill is a Skill index (see Globals). xpGained clamps to ≥ 0, and the per-hour rates return 0 until at least one second of runtime has elapsed. levelsGained counts real (unboosted) levels.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local baselined = false
script.onTick(function()
    if not baselined then srs.stats.reset(); baselined = true end
end)

script.draw(function()
    srs.overlay.new_frame()
    if srs.overlay.begin_panel("stats", "Session", Skill.Woodcutting) then
        srs.overlay.stat_row(Skill.Woodcutting, "WC xp",
            srs.overlay.short(srs.stats.xpGained(Skill.Woodcutting)))
        srs.overlay.stat_row(Skill.Woodcutting, "xp/hr",
            srs.overlay.short(math.floor(srs.stats.xpPerHour(Skill.Woodcutting))))
        srs.overlay.label("runtime " .. srs.overlay.runtime(srs.stats.runtime()))
    end
    srs.overlay.end_panel()
end)

docs.title: Tab
docs.text:
srs.tab

Authoritative source for "which sidebar tab is open right now".

Tab state lives in client variable (varc) 171. Reading it is stricter than the open-iface map (which only says the inventory IfType is loaded, not that it's the active tab).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Lua Current tab enum srs.tab.current() → integer Is given tab open srs.tab.isOpen(tab) → boolean Switch to tab srs.tab.switchTo(tab) → boolean Raw varc value srs.tab.rawIndex() → integer Virtual-key code of the tab's bound hotkey srs.tab.hotkeyVk(tab) → integer

docs.title: switchTo contract
docs.text:
1. UNKNOWN and NOTHING_SELECTED are not valid targets → return false.
  2. If current() == tab → return true immediately (no-op).
  3. Otherwise it drives the chrome tab widget (the sidebar stone), not a hotkey. The chrome (group, child) pair is resolved from the live display mode (Fixed=548 / ResizableClassic=161 / ResizableModern=164). Preferred path: fire the stone's own click action and run its handler, exactly as a hand-click would. If that handler can't be located, fall back to a synthetic left-click on the stone (this fallback returns true without confirming the switch).
  4. Returns false if the stone isn't in the current render snapshot.

A switch costs one action slot and lands on a later frame — poll current() (or isOpen()) rather than assuming it took effect the same tick.

hotkeyVk is informational only: switchTo never presses the bound key. It returns 0 if unbound (or if the varbit snapshot hasn't refreshed yet) and is useful for "Inventory tab bound to: F4" UI.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
InterfaceTab (srs.tab.*):

Lua const Value Tab UNKNOWN -1 VarClient not ready / pre-login NOTHING_SELECTED 0 No tab (fullscreen interface up) COMBAT 1 Combat SKILLS 2 Skills QUESTS 3 Quests INVENTORY 4 Inventory EQUIPMENT 5 Equipment PRAYER 6 Prayer MAGIC 7 Magic CHAT_CHANNEL 8 Chat channel FRIENDS 9 Friends ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT 10 Account management LOGOUT 11 Logout SETTINGS 12 Settings EMOTES 13 Emotes MUSIC 14 Music

Raw varc values don't match enum

The underlying varc value is 0-based and DOES NOT match this enum's ordinal; current() converts it for you (use rawIndex() only if you need the raw value). Raw values, e.g. Combat=0, Inventory=3, AccMan=8, Friends=9, Logout=10. A raw value of -1 means "no tab selected" (fullscreen interface up) and current() reports it as NOTHING_SELECTED; current() returns UNKNOWN when the varc isn't readable yet (pre-login).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if not srs.tab.isOpen(srs.tab.INVENTORY) then
    srs.tab.switchTo(srs.tab.INVENTORY)
end

docs.title: Tile
docs.text:
srs.tile

Collision queries against the active scene CollisionMap. Coordinates are world tile coords. Plane defaults to 0 (ground).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:

docs.title: isReachable — same-floor / can-I-path-there test
docs.text:
Flood-fill from the player's current tile over the live collision map (canTraverse edges); the tile is reachable iff the fill reaches it. The fill is cached per (player tile, scene, collision update), so many queries in one tick share one computation and it rebuilds when the live collision changes.

This is the correct test where plane can't help. The classic case is the Motherlode Mine: its upper level is plane 0 exactly like the ground floor, but the two are only joined by a ladder — so an upper-floor ore vein / hopper is not walk-reachable from the lower floor and isReachable returns false for it. Filter object candidates through isReachable instead of trusting plane.

Returns false pre-scene, off-scene, or when plane differs from the player's current plane (a different plane needs a transport, not a walk).

-- Only mine veins we can actually path to (skips the floor above us).
local reachable = {}
for _, v in ipairs(srs.gameobject.byId(26661)) do
    if srs.tile.isReachable(v.tileX, v.tileY, v.plane) then
        reachable[#reachable + 1] = v
    end
end

docs.title: height — render height for floor detection
docs.text:
Engine render height at the tile's SW corner, in world units. Where plane is ambiguous (MLM again — both floors are plane 0), the height differs by hundreds of units, so comparing the player's tile height against a threshold tells the floors apart (a -490 cutoff works). nil pre-scene / off-scene.

For higher-level pathing (multi-tile A*, transports, stall recovery) use Walk instead — Tile is for spot collision checks.

docs.title: Walk
docs.text:
srs.walk + legacy game.* walkers

Navigation API covering full pathfinding, single-tile clicks, and safe-tile selection. Two Lua namespaces exist side by side:

  • srs.walk — the walk facade (to / cancel / isMoving / hasArrived / state / arrivalDistance).
  • game.* — legacy walkers (moveTo, walkTo, minimapWalkTo, walkFastCanvas, walkSmart, findSafeTile, isWalkable). They drive the same path executor but are not routed through srs.walk.

All calls are safe no-ops (returning false / true depending on intent) when the executor isn't wired (pre-init host).

docs.title: srs.walk.to overloads (Lua)
docs.text:
srs.walk.to has five overloads — the type of the third argument (bool, int or table) disambiguates:

srs.walk.to(x, y)                        -- current floor, transports on
srs.walk.to(x, y, useTransports)         -- bool arg 3
srs.walk.to(x, y, plane)                 -- int arg 3: cross-plane
srs.walk.to(x, y, useTransports, plane)  -- full form
srs.walk.to(x, y, { transports = true, plane = -1, teleports = true, bank = false })  -- options table

plane 0..3 routes via stairs/ladders to the target floor; -1 means the current floor.

The options table form takes four optional fields: transports (default true), plane (default -1), teleports (default true) and bank (default false). game.moveTo(x, y, opts) accepts the same table.

docs.title: Controlling teleports
docs.text:
teleports = false keeps stairs, ladders, doors, shortcuts and fixed networks (fairy rings, spirit trees, gliders, levers, portals) but never plans an item, spell, home or minigame teleport. transports = false still means walk-only, regardless of teleports.

-- Walk to the bank, using doors/stairs/fairy rings but no teleport items or spells.
srs.walk.to(3185, 3436, { teleports = false })

docs.title: Bank routing (opt-in)
docs.text:
bank = true lets the route stop at a bank on the way to take out a teleport item (tablet, jewellery) or the runes for a teleport spell that gets the player closer, then walk the rest. It is off by default, so existing walks keep their routes.

  • The planner uses the last-known bank contents. If no bank has been opened this session, the route may stop at a nearby bank just to look, but only when that could save a long walk; it then re-plans with what the bank holds and never looks again in that session.
  • Only what the route needs is withdrawn. Nothing is ever deposited, and with a full inventory bank stops are skipped.
  • If the bank visit fails, the walk carries on without bank stops.
  • Requirement filtering still applies: a withdrawn item is only planned when the account can use it (level, quest, members world).
-- Lumbridge to Ardougne: may bank for an Ardougne teleport tablet on the way.
srs.walk.to(2662, 3305, { bank = true })

docs.title: state / arrivalDistance
docs.text:
state reports the walk lifecycle as a string: "idle", "waitingForPath", "walking", "arrived", "unreachable". Unreachable means the walk terminated without arriving — pick a different goal; don't retry the same one in a loop.

arrivalDistance is the Chebyshev distance to the goal at the moment the most recent walk arrived: 0 = exact tile, > 0 = settled nearby, -1 = no walk has arrived yet.

docs.title: Which dispatch should I use?
docs.text: Scenario Use Long-distance navigation, may need transports/multi-leg srs.walk.to / game.moveTo Force minimap clicks (long-haul behavior even close-up) game.minimapWalkTo Force canvas clicks throughout the path game.walkTo Short, time-critical dodge (1–2 ticks, single tile) game.walkFastCanvas "Just get me there, I don't care how" game.walkSmart Pick the closest safe tile, then walk there game.findSafeTile + game.walkSmart

docs.title: walkFastCanvas — single-click, no client pathfinding
docs.text:
Fires one canvas "Walk here" click at the destination tile and returns immediately. The OSRS server resolves the route, the client does no A*.

Use this for short, time-critical movements where you need a single click to fire on the current tick (dodging a falling-rocks tile, side-stepping a tick-attack hitbox).

Behavior:

  • Returns false if the tile is off-viewport (the engine can't click what it can't see). Camera angle matters — tiles behind the player or above the screen edge don't project.
  • No path validation. If a wall sits between you and the target, the server walks around it (or refuses); the client has no opinion.
  • No arrival polling. It's fire-and-forget. Re-check srs.player.position() next tick if you need to confirm.
  • plane defaults to the player's current plane.
-- Side-step east by one tile, immediately.
local p = srs.player.position()
game.walkFastCanvas(p.x + 1, p.y, p.plane)

docs.title: walkSmart — automatic dispatch
docs.text:
Picks walkFastCanvas if the target tile projects onto the canvas, otherwise falls back to the hybrid path executor (the same walker as game.moveTo). The fallback is always a current-floor walk — plane only applies to the on-canvas click.

-- Caller doesn't need to know whether the tile is visible.
game.walkSmart(targetX, targetY)

Returns true if a walk was dispatched. Useful when you have a target tile from some computation (findSafeTile, a script's own planning, etc.) and don't care which dispatch path is used.

docs.title: findSafeTile — pick the closest walkable tile not in danger
docs.text:
Searches outward by Chebyshev distance from (originX, originY) for the closest tile that satisfies all of:

  1. Not in the dangerTiles list (plane-aware match).
  2. Walkable according to the live collision map.
  3. Preferably on the current canvas (one-click reachable).

The origin tile itself is skipped — call this when the origin is the problem. An on-canvas safe tile anywhere within the radius beats a closer off-canvas one (so the result can usually be reached via walkFastCanvas). If the search exhausts without finding any on-canvas safe tile, the closest off-canvas safe tile is returned (so walkSmart can fall back to the path executor for the multi-tick approach).

Arguments:

Arg Default Notes originX, originY — Where to search around (usually the player's current tile). dangerTiles — List of {x=, y=, plane=} tables. plane defaults to the search plane if omitted. radius 5 Search radius in tiles (Chebyshev). Capped at 32. plane -1 Search plane. -1 uses the player's current plane.

Returns — a table, or nil if no candidate met the constraints:

{ x=…, y=…, plane=…, onCanvas=true|false, walkable=true }

local p = srs.player.position()
local danger = { {x=p.x, y=p.y, plane=p.plane} }  -- I'm standing on it
local safe = game.findSafeTile(p.x, p.y, danger, 3)
if safe then
    game.walkSmart(safe.x, safe.y, safe.plane)
end

docs.title: to — full pathfinder
docs.text:
The full navigation API. Plans a route with PathfinderV2 (a graph search over the bundled collision and transport data; the older v1 StaticPathfinder is the automatic fallback if that data isn't loaded) and executes it with hybrid minimap/canvas clicks across multiple ticks. Handles transports automatically. Both planners feed the same executor, so click selection, door handling and stall recovery behave identically.

  • useTransports = true (default): doors, agility shortcuts, fairy rings, manholes, ladders, etc. are invoked as the path crosses them. Set false to force a walk-only path (free accounts, missing quest reqs).
  • teleports = false excludes item, spell, home and minigame teleports while leaving other transports available.
  • bank = true allows a bank stop to withdraw a teleport item or runes — see Bank routing.
  • Without a plane argument the walk targets the player's current floor. Pass a plane argument (0..3) to route via stairs/ladders to another floor; -1 = current floor.
  • hasArrived() is true only once a walk has arrived (the executor reached the goal or got as close as it can, within about 5 tiles). It is false before any walk has been issued, while walking, and after an Unreachable termination — poll srs.walk.state() to tell "arrived" from "gave up", and srs.walk.arrivalDistance() for how close the arrival actually got.
srs.walk.to(3210, 3210)
-- … later ticks …
if srs.walk.hasArrived() then
    doStuffAtDestination()
end

docs.title: Transports (full pathfinder only)
docs.text:
When useTransports = true, the executor handles:

  • Live object-tile resolution. The transport-table origin column is the player STAND tile, not the LocType's actual tile (the object often sits 1 tile off). The walker queries the live scene by object id at fire time so OPLOC1 packets aren't silently rejected.
  • Multi-step transport chains. Manholes (Open → Climb-down), levers-then-doors, and similar two-row entries with the same origin+destination are emitted as a chain. The walker advances through them when it detects the live object's id has flipped to the next step.
  • Recalculation on completion. After any transport (success or timeout), the executor re-plans from the player's actual landing tile.
  • Boats and ships. Fixed boat and ship routes are planned like any other transport, including trips run by an NPC whose option names the destination. Routes that need a conversation first (talking to a captain) and charter ships are not planned.

Requirement filtering (PathfinderV2). Before each plan the client snapshots what your account can actually use — boosted skill levels, finished quests, items carried or worn (plus the last-known bank contents), relevant varbits/varps and whether you are on a members world — and only plans through transports whose requirements pass. Agility shortcuts, teleport items and teleport spells are therefore skipped when you lack the level, quest, item or runes. Only transport types the executor knows how to fire are planned. If the snapshot isn't available yet (e.g. just after login), any transport with a requirement is refused rather than assumed.

Pass useTransports = false to force a walk-only path regardless (for example to avoid a transport you do not want to use).

The executor also waits for an in-flight door "Open" to complete before issuing further walk clicks, skips doors that are already open (re-clicking would close them), and only opens a door the route actually crosses.

Instances. srs.walk.to translates wiki/template coordinates into the live instance's coordinates when you are inside an instance, so scripts can pass the template tile. The legacy game.* walkers do not perform this translation.

walkFastCanvas does not invoke transports — it's a one-shot canvas click, so anything more elaborate than "click this tile" needs the full pathfinder.

docs.title: Widget
docs.text:
srs.widget

Read-only inspection of the OSRS interface tree, plus a generic click. Widgets are identified by (groupId, childId).

docs.title: State / lookup
docs.text: Method Lua IfTypeManager warmed up srs.widget.isReady() → bool Find by (group, child) srs.widget.find(g, c) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil All in group srs.widget.group(g) → table Dynamic children srs.widget.dynamicChildren(g, c) → table Readable label srs.widget.label(g, c) → string

docs.title: Dynamic children
docs.text:
dynamicChildren enumerates the runtime-allocated children held by a parent widget. This is where inventory slots, bank items, dialogue options, etc. live; they don't appear in group() (which only walks the static Components array).

Each entry's dynIndex carries its array slot, parentGroupId/parentChildId point to (g, c), and text typically holds the option label or item-derived caption.

docs.title: label
docs.text:
Returns the most informative form available, in priority order:

  1. "Inventory.ITEMS" — exact InterfaceID nested constant
  2. "INVENTORY[0]" — group name + child index
  3. "149.0" — numeric fallback

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text:
Method Lua Interface rendering srs.widget.isOpen(g) → bool Drawn last frame srs.widget.isVisible(g, c) → bool Hidden (or ancestor hidden) srs.widget.isHidden(g, c) → bool Wait until rendered (poll) srs.widget.waitVisible(g, c, timeoutMs) → bool

isVisible returns true iff the engine actually drew the widget last frame (hook-snapshot path). The renderer skips any widget whose own or any ancestor's Hidden flag is set, so this matches a recursive "hidden or any ancestor hidden" check for free.

Defaults on lookup-miss:

  • isVisible(g, c) → false when widget can't be found
  • isHidden(g, c) → true when widget can't be found

waitVisible polls until (g, c) is actually rendered or timeoutMs elapses, returning the final visibility. Use it to gate keyboard entry on a prompt being open — typing into an unrendered box is silently dropped.

docs.title: Hit-test
docs.text:
Method Lua Hit-test screen point srs.widget.atPoint(sx, sy) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil Currently hovered srs.widget.hovered() → WidgetSnapshot \| nil

Rect fields are absolute screen coords for these two methods.

docs.title: Scrolling
docs.text:
Method Lua Read scroll position srs.widget.scrollY(g, c) → int \| nil Write scroll position srs.widget.setScrollY(g, c, y) → bool

scrollY reads a scrollable widget's vertical scroll offset (nil if it isn't resolved / allocated yet). setScrollY writes it — the engine picks it up on the next render frame. It is a plain write: negative values clamp to 0, but there is no upper clamp, so keep y within the widget's scrollable range yourself. The visible scrollbar thumb is painted by a separate CS2 script we don't invoke, so the thumb may look stale until the mouse moves, but items inside the viewport reflect the new offset immediately. Backs srs.bank.scrollToSlot.

docs.title: Click
docs.text:
Method Lua Click action srs.widget.click(g, c, action) → bool Click a specific op (X-aware) srs.widget.clickOp(g, c, op, actionIndex, action[, itemId=-1]) → bool Real-input click (whole widget) srs.widget.clickReal(g, c) → bool Real-input click (dynamic child) srs.widget.clickRealDynChild(g, c, dynIndex) → bool Real-input click (sub-rect) srs.widget.clickRealAt(g, c, dx, dy, w, h) → bool

click resolves the widget's absolute screen rect as currently rendered, picks a random point inside it, and routes through Interact (always-on spoof). For inventory slots prefer srs.inventory.interact — same mechanism, narrower API.

clickOp is the X-aware sibling of click: it exposes the two action fields click hard-codes — op (the menu sub-op selector; -1 = none) and actionIndex (the spawn index; 1 for almost all widget actions, 2 for GE coin-collect). itemId carries the item context (-1 for plain buttons). The action string is used only for the click's label and the ~600 ms dedupe key (keyed on the widget, op and action), so space repeated identical sub-op clicks ≥ 1 tick apart. clickOp resolves the static (g, c): aimed at a dynamic child it will no-op — use the clickReal* family for those.

Clicking Grand Exchange buttons

Some CS2 buttons — every Grand Exchange offer / stepper / confirm / collect button — need the engine to build their hover context itself, so a synthesized action no-ops on them. Use the clickReal* family (drives the real WndProc input pipeline — a curved WM_MOUSEMOVE then WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP to a random point in the rect; focus-independent and background / multi-client safe). The clickReal* calls block until the move + click finishes and return false if the widget isn't rendered this frame. clickRealDynChild targets a parent-relative dynamic child (search-result rows, side-inventory cells, steppers); clickRealAt targets a widget-relative sub-rect (icons that aren't separately hit-testable, e.g. an empty GE box's Buy icon). These mostly back the Grand Exchange facade — prefer that surface.

Field Type Notes groupId integer childId integer parentGroupId integer -1 if no parent parentChildId integer -1 if no parent dynIndex integer -1 = static child; ≥ 0 = dynamic-child slot x, y integer Parent-relative for find/group; absolute screen for atPoint/hovered width, height integer hidden boolean itemId integer -1 if not an item-bearing widget itemQty integer spriteId integer -1 if no sprite name string Tooltip name baked into the IfType text string Visible label content targetVerb string Spell/use prefix shown on cursor while staging actions table (array of string) Right-click options (first 5 only; overflow not fetched). docs.text:
if srs.widget.isReady() then
    local w = srs.widget.find(149, 0)                    -- inventory container
    if w then
        log.info(("%s: %d dynamic children"):format(
            srs.widget.label(149, 0), w.dynChildCount))
        -- inventory slots live as dynamic children of (149, 0)
        for _, slot in ipairs(srs.widget.dynamicChildren(149, 0)) do
            -- slot.itemId / slot.itemQty / slot.dynIndex per slot
        end
    end
end

docs.title: World
docs.text:
srs.world

Current world / server number.

The world number (e.g. 302, 398) as the client currently has it. Reads -1 when it isn't available yet — check srs.game.isLoggedIn() before trusting it.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Current world id srs.world.getId() → integer Seamless world hop srs.world.hopTo(world) → boolean

getId returns -1 if the client state isn't available yet or the value is the pre-login sentinel.

hopTo performs a seamless in-game world switch (the native world-switcher — no logout). The current game version only honours a hop while the World Switcher is open, so if it isn't showing, hopTo first switches to the Logout tab, clicks "World Switcher" and waits for it to open. That step blocks the calling script thread for up to ~5 seconds and leaves the Logout tab selected. The hop itself is then scheduled onto the engine main thread, so the call returns as soon as the hop is accepted, not when the new world finishes loading — poll srs.world.getId() / srs.game.state() for completion. Returns false (nothing scheduled) when not logged in, when world is the current world, when world isn't a known world, or when the engine isn't resolved. Must be logged in; for a members world the account must be a member (the engine silently rejects ineligible targets).

docs.title: World directory
docs.text:
Read the engine's world list to pick a hop target by population / activity / type instead of a hard-coded number.

Method Lua One world by number srs.world.get(world) → WorldInfo\|nil Whole list srs.world.all() → WorldInfo[]

WorldInfo (a table; read-only copy):

Field Type Notes id integer world number population integer live player count; -1 if not yet received region string "United States" / "United Kingdom" / "Australia" / "Germany" / "Unknown" location integer raw region code (0=US, 1=UK, 3=AU, 7=DE) members boolean members world (flags & 0x1) pvp boolean PvP world (flags & 0x4) highRisk boolean high-risk world (flags & 0x400) flags integer raw world-type mask — check other bits yourself if needed host string server host / address activity string activity label ("Trade", "Wintertodt", "1500 skill total", …)

Field semantics not yet live-verified

The WorldInfo field decoding (flags, members, pvp, highRisk, …) is derived from the client's world-list layout and has not been confirmed in-game on the current build — treat flags-derived booleans as best-effort.

Empty until the world list loads

The engine only populates the world list once the world-switcher is opened (or shortly after login). Before that, all() returns an empty table and get() returns nil. all() probes the engine resolver across the world-number range, so call it sparingly (e.g. once when choosing a hop target), never per tick.

-- pick the least-populated non-PvP, non-high-risk members world in your region
local best, bestPop = nil, math.huge
for _, w in ipairs(srs.world.all()) do
    if w.members and not w.pvp and not w.highRisk
       and w.region == "United States"          -- your region
       and w.population >= 0 and w.population < bestPop then
        best, bestPop = w.id, w.population
    end
end
if best then srs.world.hopTo(best) end

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if srs.world.getId() ~= 302 then
    if srs.world.hopTo(302) then
        log.info("hop to 302 accepted — waiting for completion")
    end
end
